verses.rationale: Keeps genesis/origins broader than a mere name list and preserves the two defining ancestral titles.
verses.before: The record of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, son of David, son of Abraham:
verses.after: The record of the origins of Jesus the Messiah, son of David, son of Abraham.
verses.tsw_comparator: The book of the genealogy of Jesus the Messiah, son of David, son of Abraham.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated begetting pattern and Judah’s brothers.
verses.before: Abraham was the father of Isaac, Isaac the father of Jacob, and Jacob the father of Judah and his brothers.
verses.after: Abraham fathered Isaac; Isaac fathered Jacob; Jacob fathered Judah and his brothers.
verses.tsw_comparator: Abraham fathered Isaac, and Isaac fathered Jacob, and Jacob fathered Judah and his brothers,

verses.rationale: Preserves both twins, mother, and exact sequence.
verses.before: Judah was the father of Perez and Zerah by Tamar; Perez the father of Hezron; Hezron the father of Ram;
verses.after: Judah fathered Perez and Zerah by Tamar; Perez fathered Hezron; Hezron fathered Ram.
verses.tsw_comparator: and Judah fathered Perez and Zerah by Tamar, and Perez fathered Hezron, and Hezron fathered Ram,

verses.rationale: Keeps the three linked generations in the same cadence.
verses.before: Ram the father of Amminadab; Amminadab the father of Nahshon; Nahshon the father of Salmon;
verses.after: Ram fathered Amminadab; Amminadab fathered Nahshon; Nahshon fathered Salmon.
verses.tsw_comparator: and Ram fathered Amminadab, and Amminadab fathered Nahshon, and Nahshon fathered Salmon,

verses.rationale: Retains both named women and every relationship.
verses.before: Salmon the father of Boaz by Rahab; Boaz the father of Obed by Ruth; Obed the father of Jesse;
verses.after: Salmon fathered Boaz by Rahab; Boaz fathered Obed by Ruth; Obed fathered Jesse.
verses.tsw_comparator: and Salmon fathered Boaz by Rahab, and Boaz fathered Obed by Ruth, and Obed fathered Jesse,

verses.rationale: Keeps king attached to David and the deliberate identification through Uriah rather than supplying Bathsheba.
verses.before: and Jesse the father of King David. David was the father of Solomon by the wife of Uriah;
verses.after: Jesse fathered David the king. David fathered Solomon by Uriah’s wife.
verses.tsw_comparator: and Jesse fathered David the king. And David fathered Solomon by the wife of Uriah,

verses.rationale: Follows pinned Asaph rather than harmonizing to Asa.
verses.before: Solomon the father of Rehoboam; Rehoboam the father of Abijah; Abijah the father of Asaph;
verses.after: Solomon fathered Rehoboam; Rehoboam fathered Abijah; Abijah fathered Asaph.
verses.tsw_comparator: and Solomon fathered Rehoboam, and Rehoboam fathered Abijah, and Abijah fathered Asa,

verses.rationale: Retains the source’s compressed genealogy without inserting omitted kings.
verses.before: Asaph the father of Jehoshaphat; Jehoshaphat the father of Joram; Joram the father of Uzziah;
verses.after: Asaph fathered Jehoshaphat; Jehoshaphat fathered Joram; Joram fathered Uzziah.
verses.tsw_comparator: and Asa fathered Jehoshaphat, and Jehoshaphat fathered Joram, and Joram fathered Uzziah,

verses.rationale: Preserves the three royal links and established names.
verses.before: Uzziah the father of Jotham; Jotham the father of Ahaz; Ahaz the father of Hezekiah;
verses.after: Uzziah fathered Jotham; Jotham fathered Ahaz; Ahaz fathered Hezekiah.
verses.tsw_comparator: and Uzziah fathered Jotham, and Jotham fathered Ahaz, and Ahaz fathered Hezekiah,

verses.rationale: Follows pinned Amos rather than harmonizing to Amon.
verses.before: Hezekiah the father of Manasseh; Manasseh the father of Amos; Amos the father of Josiah;
verses.after: Hezekiah fathered Manasseh; Manasseh fathered Amos; Amos fathered Josiah.
verses.tsw_comparator: and Hezekiah fathered Manasseh, and Manasseh fathered Amos, and Amos fathered Josiah,

verses.rationale: Keeps the deportation hinge and the source’s brothers.
verses.before: and Josiah the father of Jeconiah and his brothers at the time of the exile to Babylon.
verses.after: Josiah fathered Jeconiah and his brothers at the time of the deportation to Babylon.
verses.tsw_comparator: and Josiah fathered Jechoniah and his brothers at the time of the deportation to Babylon.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated historical hinge before the next generation group.
verses.before: After the exile to Babylon: Jeconiah was the father of Shealtiel; Shealtiel the father of Zerubbabel;
verses.after: After the deportation to Babylon, Jeconiah fathered Shealtiel; Shealtiel fathered Zerubbabel.
verses.tsw_comparator: And after the deportation to Babylon: Jechoniah fathered Shealtiel, and Shealtiel fathered Zerubbabel,

verses.rationale: Preserves all three otherwise unexplained links.
verses.before: Zerubbabel the father of Abiud; Abiud the father of Eliakim; Eliakim the father of Azor;
verses.after: Zerubbabel fathered Abiud; Abiud fathered Eliakim; Eliakim fathered Azor.
verses.tsw_comparator: and Zerubbabel fathered Abiud, and Abiud fathered Eliakim, and Eliakim fathered Azor,

verses.rationale: Maintains the genealogy’s deliberately repeated cadence.
verses.before: Azor the father of Zadok; Zadok the father of Achim; Achim the father of Eliud;
verses.after: Azor fathered Zadok; Zadok fathered Achim; Achim fathered Eliud.
verses.tsw_comparator: and Azor fathered Zadok, and Zadok fathered Achim, and Achim fathered Eliud,

verses.rationale: Retains the exact final three links before Joseph.
verses.before: Eliud the father of Eleazar; Eleazar the father of Matthan; Matthan the father of Jacob;
verses.after: Eliud fathered Eleazar; Eleazar fathered Matthan; Matthan fathered Jacob.
verses.tsw_comparator: and Eliud fathered Eleazar, and Eleazar fathered Matthan, and Matthan fathered Jacob,

verses.rationale: Makes the feminine from-whom referent explicit and preserves the switch to passive birth.
verses.before: and Jacob the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary, from whom Jesus was born, who is called Christ.
verses.after: Jacob fathered Joseph, Mary’s husband. From her was born Jesus, who is called the Messiah.
verses.tsw_comparator: and Jacob fathered Joseph the husband of Mary, from whom Jesus was born, who is called the Messiah.

verses.rationale: Retains all three fourteens and historical boundaries without repairing the literary count.
verses.before: So all the generations from Abraham to David were fourteen generations; from David to the exile to Babylon, fourteen generations; and from the exile to Babylon to the Christ, fourteen generations.
verses.after: So there were fourteen generations from Abraham to David, fourteen from David to the deportation to Babylon, and fourteen from the deportation to Babylon to the Messiah.
verses.tsw_comparator: So all the generations from Abraham to David were fourteen generations, and from David to the deportation to Babylon fourteen generations, and from the deportation to Babylon to the Messiah fourteen generations.

verses.rationale: Preserves binding betrothal, prior-to-union timing, and divine agency.
verses.before: This is how the birth of Jesus Christ took place. His mother Mary had been pledged in marriage to Joseph, but before they came together she was found to be pregnant through the Holy Spirit.
verses.after: This is how the birth of Jesus the Messiah came about. His mother Mary was pledged in marriage to Joseph, but before they came together she was found to be pregnant through the Holy Spirit.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the birth of Jesus the Messiah was in this way: when his mother Mary had been betrothed to Joseph, before they came together she was found to be with child from the Holy Spirit.

verses.rationale: Keeps righteousness alongside restraint and renders the legal separation clearly.
verses.before: Joseph her husband was righteous and did not want to expose her publicly, so he planned to divorce her quietly.
verses.after: Her husband Joseph was righteous and did not want to expose her to public disgrace, so he decided to divorce her quietly.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Joseph her husband, being righteous and not willing to expose her to public shame, resolved to divorce her quietly.

verses.rationale: Keeps Davidic address, dream, and conception’s source.
verses.before: But after he had considered this, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, “Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife, because what has been conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.
verses.after: While he was considering this, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream. “Joseph, son of David,” he said, “do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife. The child conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.
verses.tsw_comparator: But as he considered these things, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, “Joseph, son of David, do not fear to take Mary as your wife, for what is conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.

verses.rationale: Preserves Joseph’s naming responsibility and salvation from sins, with name-wordplay noted.
verses.before: She will give birth to a son, and you will name him Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins.”
verses.after: She will bear a son, and you must name him Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins.”
verses.tsw_comparator: She will bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.”

verses.rationale: Retains the first fulfillment formula and both divine and prophetic agency.
verses.before: All this happened to fulfill what the Lord had spoken through the prophet:
verses.after: All this happened to fulfill what the Lord had spoken through the prophet:
verses.tsw_comparator: All this took place to fulfill what the Lord had spoken by the prophet:

verses.rationale: Follows Matthew’s Greek virgin and plural they-will-name, preserving the text’s own translation.
verses.before: “Look, the virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and they will name him Emmanuel,” which means, “God with us.”
verses.after: “Look, the virgin will conceive and bear a son, and they will name him Emmanuel,” which means “God with us.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and they shall call his name Immanuel” (which means, God with us).

verses.rationale: Keeps waking, obedience, and receiving Mary as linked actions.
verses.before: When Joseph woke from sleep, he did as the angel of the Lord commanded him and took Mary as his wife.
verses.after: When Joseph woke, he did what the angel of the Lord had commanded and took his wife home.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Joseph rose from sleep and did as the angel of the Lord commanded him: he took his wife,

verses.rationale: Makes knew explicit while leaving what follows until unstated and retaining the pinned absence of firstborn.
verses.before: But he did not have sexual relations with her until she gave birth to a son. And he named him Jesus.
verses.after: But he did not have sexual relations with her until she bore a son. He named him Jesus.
verses.tsw_comparator: but he did not know her until she had borne a son. And he called his name Jesus.

verses.rationale: Retains magi without adding kings, number, or names.
verses.before: After Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of King Herod, magi from the east came to Jerusalem,
verses.after: After Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea, during King Herod’s reign, magi from the east arrived in Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now after Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king, behold, wise men from the east came to Jerusalem,

verses.rationale: Keeps born king and the rising/east ambiguity in a note; bowing does not predetermine the visitors’ theology.
verses.before: asking, “Where is the one who has been born king of the Jews? We saw his star when it rose and have come to pay him homage.”
verses.after: “Where is the one born king of the Jews?” they asked. “We saw his star at its rising and have come to bow before him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: saying, “Where is he who has been born king of the Jews? For we saw his star in the east and have come to bow down to him.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the city’s shared disturbance without inventing its motive.
verses.before: When King Herod heard this, he was disturbed, and all Jerusalem with him.
verses.after: When King Herod heard this, he was alarmed, and all Jerusalem with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when Herod the king heard this, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him,

verses.rationale: Keeps both named groups and the expected birth-location question.
verses.before: He gathered all the chief priests and scribes of the people and asked them where the Christ was to be born.
verses.after: He gathered all the people’s chief priests and scribes and asked them where the Messiah was to be born.
verses.tsw_comparator: and gathering all the chief priests and scribes of the people, he inquired of them where the Messiah was to be born.

verses.rationale: Retains the quoted scriptural basis and regional identification.
verses.before: They told him, “In Bethlehem of Judea, because this is what has been written through the prophet:
verses.after: “In Bethlehem of Judea,” they told him, “for this is what was written through the prophet:
verses.tsw_comparator: And they said to him, “In Bethlehem of Judea, for so it has been written by the prophet:

verses.rationale: Follows Matthew’s quotation rather than harmonizing its wording to Micah’s Hebrew.
verses.before: ‘And you, Bethlehem, land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah, because from you will come a ruler who will shepherd my people Israel.’”
verses.after: ‘And you, Bethlehem in Judah’s land, are by no means least among Judah’s rulers, for from you will come a ruler who will shepherd my people Israel.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘And you, Bethlehem, land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah; for from you shall come a ruler who will shepherd my people Israel.’”

verses.rationale: Preserves secrecy and precise chronological inquiry.
verses.before: Then Herod secretly called the magi and learned from them the exact time when the star had appeared.
verses.after: Then Herod secretly summoned the magi and determined from them exactly when the star had appeared.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Herod summoned the wise men secretly and determined from them the exact time the star had appeared.

verses.rationale: Keeps Herod’s professed purpose in his own speech without endorsing it.
verses.before: He sent them to Bethlehem and said, “Go and search carefully for the child. When you find him, report back to me so that I too may go and pay him homage.”
verses.after: He sent them to Bethlehem, saying, “Go and search carefully for the child. When you find him, report back to me, so I too can go and bow before him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he sent them to Bethlehem, saying, “Go and search carefully for the child, and when you have found him, bring me word, that I also may come and bow down to him.”

verses.rationale: Retains the star’s narrative movement without substituting an astronomical explanation.
verses.before: After hearing the king, they went on their way. And the star they had seen at its rising went ahead of them until it came and stood over the place where the child was.
verses.after: After hearing the king, they went on their way. The star they had seen at its rising went ahead of them until it stopped over the place where the child was.
verses.tsw_comparator: And after listening to the king, they went on their way. And behold, the star they had seen in the east went before them until it came to rest over the place where the child was.

verses.rationale: Carries the piled-up Greek intensification into natural English.
verses.before: When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceedingly great joy.
verses.after: When they saw the star, they were overwhelmed with joy.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceedingly great joy.

verses.rationale: Preserves house, mother, bodily homage, and all three gifts.
verses.before: Entering the house, they saw the child with Mary his mother. They fell down and paid him homage. Then they opened their treasures and offered him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
verses.after: They entered the house and saw the child with Mary his mother. They fell down and bowed before him. Then they opened their treasure chests and offered him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
verses.tsw_comparator: And going into the house, they saw the child with Mary his mother, and they fell down and bowed down to him. Then, opening their treasures, they offered him gifts—gold and frankincense and myrrh.

verses.rationale: Retains dream warning and changed route without supplying the warning’s speaker.
verses.before: Having been warned in a dream not to return to Herod, they went back to their own country by another road.
verses.after: Warned in a dream not to return to Herod, they went home by another route.
verses.tsw_comparator: And being warned in a dream not to return to Herod, they departed to their own country by another way.

verses.rationale: Keeps flight, destination, waiting condition, and explicit threatened killing.
verses.before: After they had gone, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream and said, “Get up, take the child and his mother, flee to Egypt, and stay there until I tell you, because Herod is about to search for the child to destroy him.”
verses.after: After they left, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream. “Get up,” he said. “Take the child and his mother and flee to Egypt. Stay there until I tell you, because Herod is about to search for the child to kill him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now when they had departed, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream, saying, “Rise, take the child and his mother, and flee to Egypt, and remain there until I tell you, for Herod is about to search for the child to destroy him.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the urgent nighttime response and repeated child/mother wording.
verses.before: Joseph got up, took the child and his mother during the night, and left for Egypt.
verses.after: Joseph got up, took the child and his mother during the night, and left for Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he rose and took the child and his mother by night and departed to Egypt,

verses.rationale: Retains fulfillment and the quotation without rewriting Hosea’s earlier context.
verses.before: He stayed there until Herod's death, so that what the Lord had spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled: “Out of Egypt I called my son.”
verses.after: He stayed there until Herod’s death. This fulfilled what the Lord had spoken through the prophet: “Out of Egypt I called my son.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and remained there until the death of Herod. This was to fulfill what the Lord had spoken by the prophet: “Out of Egypt I called my son.”

verses.rationale: Preserves deliberate killing, male children, age boundary, location, and the timing link.
verses.before: When Herod realized that he had been deceived by the magi, he became furious. He sent men and killed all the boys in Bethlehem and its surrounding region who were two years old and younger, according to the time he had learned from the magi.
verses.after: When Herod realized the magi had outwitted him, he became furious. He sent men to kill all the boys in Bethlehem and the surrounding district who were two years old or younger, according to the time he had learned from the magi.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Herod, when he saw that he had been deceived by the wise men, became furious, and he sent and killed all the male children in Bethlehem and in all that region who were two years old and under, according to the time that he had determined from the wise men.

verses.rationale: Keeps named prophetic attribution.
verses.before: Then what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled:
verses.after: Then what had been spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then was fulfilled what had been spoken by the prophet Jeremiah:

verses.rationale: Preserves maternal grief and refusal of comfort without adding closure.
verses.before: “A voice was heard in Ramah, weeping and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children; she refused to be comforted, because they are no more.”
verses.after: “A voice was heard in Ramah, weeping and great mourning— Rachel weeping for her children, refusing to be comforted, because they are no more.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “A voice was heard in Ramah, weeping and loud lamentation, Rachel weeping for her children; she refused to be comforted, because they are no more.”

verses.rationale: Keeps both death transition and dream location.
verses.before: After Herod died, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt
verses.after: After Herod died, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when Herod died, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt,

verses.rationale: Retains the source’s plural those despite the immediate singular Herod reference.
verses.before: and said, “Get up, take the child and his mother, and go to the land of Israel, because those who were seeking the child's life are dead.”
verses.after: “Get up,” he said. “Take the child and his mother and go to the land of Israel, because those who sought the child’s life are dead.”
verses.tsw_comparator: saying, “Rise, take the child and his mother and go to the land of Israel, for those who sought the child’s life are dead.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the obedient repetition of the command.
verses.before: So Joseph got up, took the child and his mother, and entered the land of Israel.
verses.after: Joseph got up, took the child and his mother, and entered the land of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he rose and took the child and his mother and went to the land of Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps named succession, fear, and the second relocation warning.
verses.before: But when he heard that Archelaus was ruling Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there. After being warned in a dream, he withdrew to the region of Galilee.
verses.after: But when he heard that Archelaus ruled Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there. Warned in a dream, he withdrew to the region of Galilee.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when he heard that Archelaus was reigning over Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there, and being warned in a dream, he withdrew to the region of Galilee.

verses.rationale: Preserves plural prophets and the unassigned quotation rather than inventing a single source.
verses.before: He went and settled in a town called Nazareth, so that what was spoken through the prophets might be fulfilled: “He will be called a Nazarene.”
verses.after: He settled in a town called Nazareth, fulfilling what was spoken through the prophets: “He will be called a Nazarene.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he went and lived in a city called Nazareth, so that what had been spoken by the prophets might be fulfilled, that he would be called a Nazarene.

verses.rationale: Keeps wilderness, title, and the announcement’s narrative arrival.
verses.before: In those days John the Baptist appeared in the wilderness of Judea, proclaiming,
verses.after: In those days John the Baptist appeared in the Judean wilderness, proclaiming,
verses.tsw_comparator: In those days John the Baptizer came, proclaiming in the wilderness of Judea,

verses.rationale: Retains repentance and the kingdom’s nearness as a recurring formula.
verses.before: “Repent, because the kingdom of heaven has drawn near.”
verses.after: “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has drawn near!”
verses.tsw_comparator: saying, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has drawn near.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the quotation’s voice, wilderness, and road-preparation imagery.
verses.before: This is the one spoken of through Isaiah the prophet: “A voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Prepare the way of the Lord; make his paths straight.’”
verses.after: This is the one spoken of through Isaiah the prophet: “A voice cries out in the wilderness: ‘Prepare the Lord’s way; make his paths straight.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: For this is he who was spoken of through Isaiah the prophet, saying, “The voice of one crying in the wilderness: ‘Prepare the way of the Lord; make his paths straight.’”

verses.rationale: Retains all concrete clothing and food details without modern substitutes.
verses.before: John wore clothing made of camel's hair, with a leather belt around his waist, and his food was locusts and wild honey.
verses.after: John wore clothing made of camel’s hair and a leather belt around his waist. His food was locusts and wild honey.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now John himself wore a garment of camel’s hair and a leather belt around his waist, and his food was locusts and wild honey.

verses.rationale: Makes the geographical collective subjects natural while retaining their broad scope.
verses.before: Then Jerusalem, all Judea, and all the region around the Jordan were going out to him.
verses.after: People from Jerusalem, all Judea, and the whole Jordan region went out to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jerusalem and all Judea and all the region around the Jordan were going out to him,

verses.rationale: Keeps confession and baptism together without asserting a technical order beyond narrative flow.
verses.before: They were baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.
verses.after: They confessed their sins and were baptized by him in the Jordan River.
verses.tsw_comparator: and they were being baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.

verses.rationale: Preserves the named groups, biting insult, and question about warning.
