verses.after: When he saw many Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism, he said, “You brood of vipers! Who warned you to flee the coming wrath?
verses.tsw_comparator: But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming for baptism, he said to them, “Offspring of vipers, who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?

verses.rationale: Retains the fruit image and repentance connection.
verses.before: Produce fruit worthy of repentance.
verses.after: Produce fruit worthy of repentance.
verses.tsw_comparator: Bear fruit worthy of repentance,

verses.rationale: Keeps ancestral claim and stones/children reversal without adding a doctrine of replacement.
verses.before: Do not presume to say to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father,’ because I tell you that God is able to raise up children for Abraham from these stones.
verses.after: Do not think you can say to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father.’ I tell you, God can raise up children for Abraham from these stones.
verses.tsw_comparator: and do not presume to say within yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father,’ for I tell you that God is able from these stones to raise up children for Abraham.

verses.rationale: Preserves already, root, and the repeated fruit judgment.
verses.before: Even now the axe is lying at the root of the trees. Every tree that does not produce good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
verses.after: The ax is already lying at the trees’ root. Every tree that fails to produce good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: And even now the axe is laid to the root of the trees; therefore every tree not producing good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.

verses.rationale: Keeps water/Spirit/fire and carrying sandals rather than harmonizing to untying them.
verses.before: I baptize you with water for repentance, but the one coming after me is stronger than I am. I am not worthy to carry his sandals. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.
verses.after: I baptize you in water for repentance. But the one coming after me is stronger than I am; I am not worthy even to carry his sandals. He will baptize you in the Holy Spirit and fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: “I baptize you with water for repentance, but the one coming after me is stronger than I, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.

verses.rationale: Retains each agricultural implement/action and the fire’s unquenchability.
verses.before: His winnowing fork is in his hand. He will thoroughly clear his threshing floor and gather his wheat into the barn, but the chaff he will burn with unquenchable fire.”
verses.after: His winnowing fork is in his hand. He will clear his threshing floor and gather his wheat into the storehouse, but burn the chaff with fire that cannot be put out.”
verses.tsw_comparator: His winnowing fork is in his hand, and he will thoroughly clear his threshing floor and gather his wheat into the storehouse, but the chaff he will burn with unquenchable fire.”

verses.rationale: Keeps Jesus’ stated purpose and locations.
verses.before: Then Jesus came from Galilee to John at the Jordan to be baptized by him.
verses.after: Then Jesus came from Galilee to John at the Jordan to be baptized by him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to John, to be baptized by him.

verses.rationale: Retains John’s attempted resistance and surprised question.
verses.before: But John tried to prevent him, saying, “I need to be baptized by you, and you come to me?”
verses.after: John tried to stop him. “I need to be baptized by you,” he said, “and you come to me?”
verses.tsw_comparator: But John tried to prevent him, saying, “I need to be baptized by you, and do you come to me?”

verses.rationale: Preserves now, us, righteousness, and the repeated allowing without overexplaining the theology.
verses.before: Jesus answered him, “Let it be so now, because in this way it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness.” Then John allowed him.
verses.after: Jesus answered, “Allow it for now. This is how it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness.” Then John allowed him.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Jesus answered him, “Permit it now, for thus it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness.” Then he permitted him.

verses.rationale: Keeps the visual subject he and the dove comparison rather than declaring a literal bird.
verses.before: After Jesus was baptized, he immediately came up from the water. And look—the heavens were opened to him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and coming upon him.
verses.after: After Jesus was baptized, he immediately came up from the water. The heavens opened, and he saw God’s Spirit descending like a dove and coming upon him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when Jesus was baptized, he went up immediately from the water, and behold, the heavens were opened to him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and coming upon him.

verses.rationale: Preserves third-person public declaration and divine delight.
verses.before: And look—a voice from the heavens said, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.”
verses.after: A voice from heaven said, “This is my beloved Son; in him I delight.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And behold, a voice from the heavens said, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the Spirit’s leading and the devil’s testing as distinct roles.
verses.before: Then Jesus was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tested by the devil.
verses.after: Then the Spirit led Jesus into the wilderness to be tested by the devil.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jesus was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tested by the devil.

verses.rationale: Retains both forty periods and the bodily hunger.
verses.before: After fasting forty days and forty nights, he was hungry.
verses.after: He fasted for forty days and forty nights, and afterward he was hungry.
verses.tsw_comparator: He fasted forty days and forty nights, and afterward he was hungry.

verses.rationale: Preserves conditional challenge and plural stones/loaves.
verses.before: The tempter came and said to him, “If you are God's Son, tell these stones to become loaves of bread.”
verses.after: The tempter approached him and said, “If you are God’s Son, tell these stones to become loaves of bread.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The tempter came and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, command these stones to become loaves of bread.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the scriptural answer and mouth image with inclusive human referent.
verses.before: But Jesus answered, “It is written: ‘A person shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God.’”
verses.after: Jesus answered, “It is written, ‘A human being does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from God’s mouth.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: But he answered, “It is written, ‘One does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God.’”

verses.rationale: Retains holy city and the uncertain architectural edge without inventing a precise height.
verses.before: Then the devil took him into the holy city, set him on the highest point of the temple,
verses.after: Then the devil took him into the holy city and placed him on the temple’s high edge.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the devil took him to the holy city and placed him on the pinnacle of the temple,

verses.rationale: Preserves the devil’s scriptural citation and both quoted clauses.
verses.before: and said, “If you are God's Son, throw yourself down, because it is written: ‘He will command his angels concerning you,’ and, ‘On their hands they will lift you up, so that you do not strike your foot against a stone.’”
verses.after: “If you are God’s Son,” he said, “throw yourself down. For it is written: ‘He will command his angels concerning you,’ and, ‘They will lift you on their hands, so your foot will not strike a stone.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: saying to him, “If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down; for it is written, ‘He will command his angels concerning you,’ and ‘On their hands they will bear you up, so that you will not strike your foot against a stone.’”

verses.rationale: Retains the balancing scriptural reply and test verb.
verses.before: Jesus said to him, “Again it is written, ‘You shall not test the Lord your God.’”
verses.after: Jesus told him, “It is also written, ‘Do not put the Lord your God to the test.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Jesus said to him, “Again it is written, ‘Do not put the Lord your God to the test.’”

verses.rationale: Keeps the comprehensive kingdoms/glory offer and mountain setting.
verses.before: Again the devil took him to a very high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory.
verses.after: Again the devil took him, this time to a very high mountain, and showed him all the world’s kingdoms and their glory.
verses.tsw_comparator: Again, the devil took him to a very high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory;

verses.rationale: Retains the explicit exchange condition and bodily submission.
verses.before: He said to him, “I will give you all these things if you fall down and worship me.”
verses.after: “I will give you all of this,” he said, “if you fall down and worship me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and he said to him, “All these I will give you, if you will fall down and worship me.”

verses.rationale: Keeps Satan’s name, both worship/service verbs, and exclusive alone.
verses.before: Then Jesus said to him, “Go away, Satan! For it is written: ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and serve him alone.’”
verses.after: Jesus said, “Go away, Satan! For it is written, ‘Worship the Lord your God and serve him alone.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Jesus said to him, “Away with you, Satan! for it is written, ‘Worship the Lord your God, and serve only him.’”

verses.rationale: Retains departure followed by angelic service.
verses.before: Then the devil left him, and angels came and began serving him.
verses.after: Then the devil left him, and angels came and attended to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the devil left him, and suddenly angels came and waited on him.

verses.rationale: Preserves handed-over wording that recurs in the Gospel, with arrest context in a note.
verses.before: When Jesus heard that John had been handed over, he withdrew to Galilee.
verses.after: When Jesus heard that John had been handed over, he withdrew to Galilee.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now when Jesus heard that John had been arrested, he withdrew to Galilee.

verses.rationale: Keeps settlement, shoreline, and both tribal names.
verses.before: Leaving Nazareth, he came and lived in Capernaum by the sea, in the territory of Zebulun and Naphtali,
verses.after: He left Nazareth and settled in Capernaum beside the sea, in the territory of Zebulun and Naphtali.
verses.tsw_comparator: He left Nazareth and made his home in Capernaum by the sea, in the territory of Zebulun and Naphtali,

verses.rationale: Retains the named fulfillment introduction.
verses.before: so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled:
verses.after: This fulfilled what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet:
verses.tsw_comparator: so that what had been spoken through the prophet Isaiah might be fulfilled:

verses.rationale: Keeps every geographical element and nations rather than silently interpreting the population.
verses.before: “Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles—
verses.after: “Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the road by the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations—
verses.tsw_comparator: “Land of Zebulun, land of Naphtali, on the road by the sea, across the Jordan, Galilee of the nations—

verses.rationale: Preserves sitting repeated and light/darkness/death imagery.
verses.before: the people sitting in darkness have seen a great light, and for those sitting in the land and shadow of death, light has dawned.”
verses.after: the people sitting in darkness have seen a great light; for those sitting in the land and shadow of death, light has dawned.”
verses.tsw_comparator: the people who sat in darkness have seen a great light, and for those who sat in the region and shadow of death light has dawned.”

verses.rationale: Repeats John’s proclamation exactly to preserve narrative continuity.
verses.before: From that time Jesus began to proclaim, “Repent, because the kingdom of heaven has drawn near.”
verses.after: From then on Jesus began to proclaim, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has drawn near!”
verses.tsw_comparator: From that time Jesus began to proclaim, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.”

verses.rationale: Retains both names, kinship, and fishing action.
verses.before: As Jesus was walking beside the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers: Simon, called Peter, and his brother Andrew. They were casting a net into the sea, because they were fishermen.
verses.after: Walking beside the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers, Simon called Peter and his brother Andrew, casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
verses.tsw_comparator: As he walked by the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea—for they were fishermen.

verses.rationale: Preserves the fishing metaphor and inclusive object without replacing it with recruitment explanation.
verses.before: He said to them, “Come after me, and I will make you fishers of people.”
verses.after: “Come after me,” he said, “and I will make you fishers of people.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to them, “Follow me, and I will make you fish for people.”

verses.rationale: Keeps immediate response and concrete abandoned equipment.
verses.before: Immediately they left their nets and followed him.
verses.after: At once they left their nets and followed him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Immediately they left their nets and followed him.

verses.rationale: Retains the full family scene and net-mending work.
verses.before: Going on from there, he saw two other brothers, James son of Zebedee and his brother John, in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets. He called them,
verses.after: Going farther, he saw two more brothers, James son of Zebedee and his brother John. They were in the boat with their father Zebedee, mending their nets. He called them,
verses.tsw_comparator: As he went on from there, he saw two other brothers, James son of Zebedee and John his brother, in the boat with their father Zebedee, mending their nets, and he called them.

verses.rationale: Keeps both things left and the repeated immediate following.
verses.before: and immediately they left the boat and their father and followed him.
verses.after: and at once they left the boat and their father and followed him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Immediately they left the boat and their father, and followed him.

verses.rationale: Retains teaching/proclamation/healing as three distinct activities.
verses.before: Jesus went throughout all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, proclaiming the good news of the kingdom, and healing every disease and every sickness among the people.
verses.after: He traveled throughout Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, proclaiming the good news of the kingdom, and healing every disease and illness among the people.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jesus went throughout Galilee, teaching in their synagogues and proclaiming the good news of the kingdom and curing every disease and every sickness among the people.

verses.rationale: Preserves the distinct afflictions without conflating seizures with demonic possession.
verses.before: News about him spread throughout all Syria. They brought to him everyone suffering from various diseases and severe pains, those oppressed by demons, those having seizures, and those who were paralyzed, and he healed them.
verses.after: Word about him spread throughout Syria. People brought him everyone suffering from various diseases and severe pain, those afflicted by demons, those with seizures, and those who were paralyzed. He healed them.
verses.tsw_comparator: So his fame spread throughout all Syria, and they brought to him all the sick, those afflicted with various diseases and pains, demoniacs, epileptics, and paralytics, and he cured them.

verses.rationale: Keeps all five places and the broad following.
verses.before: Large crowds followed him from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and beyond the Jordan.
verses.after: Large crowds followed him from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and beyond the Jordan.
verses.tsw_comparator: And great crowds followed him from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and from beyond the Jordan.

verses.rationale: Keeps setting, teaching posture, and distinct disciples within the crowd scene.
verses.before: When Jesus saw the crowds, he went up the mountain. After he sat down, his disciples came to him.
verses.after: When Jesus saw the crowds, he went up the mountain and sat down. His disciples came to him,
verses.tsw_comparator: When Jesus saw the crowds, he went up the mountain; and after he sat down, his disciples came to him.

verses.rationale: Renders opened-his-mouth as the beginning of formal speech.
verses.before: He began teaching them:
verses.after: and he began to teach them:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he began to speak, and taught them, saying:

verses.rationale: Retains the qualification in spirit and present possession rather than paraphrasing the blessing.
verses.before: “Blessed are the poor in spirit, because theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
verses.after: “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for the kingdom of heaven is theirs.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

verses.rationale: Keeps mourning broad and the passive future comfort.
verses.before: Blessed are those who mourn, because they will be comforted.
verses.after: Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.

verses.rationale: Renders praus as gentle with meekness noted, retaining inheritance and earth/land range.
verses.before: Blessed are the meek, because they will inherit the earth.
verses.after: Blessed are the gentle, for they will inherit the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth.

verses.rationale: Preserves both bodily desires and righteousness as a recurring term.
verses.before: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, because they will be filled.
verses.after: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be filled.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be filled.

verses.rationale: Keeps the mercy reciprocity with clear passive sense.
verses.before: Blessed are the merciful, because they will receive mercy.
verses.after: Blessed are the merciful, for they will receive mercy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed are the merciful, for they will receive mercy.

verses.rationale: Retains heart and seeing without adding an explanation of purity.
verses.before: Blessed are the pure in heart, because they will see God.
verses.after: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.

verses.rationale: Uses children for the inclusive human group while retaining the divine-family image.
verses.before: Blessed are the peacemakers, because they will be called children of God.
verses.after: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called God’s children.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.

verses.rationale: Matches the opening kingdom promise and retains persecution’s stated cause.
verses.before: Blessed are those who are persecuted because of righteousness, because theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
verses.after: Blessed are those persecuted for righteousness, for the kingdom of heaven is theirs.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed are those who are persecuted for righteousness’ sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

verses.rationale: Keeps the shift to direct address, falsity, and because-of-me qualification.
verses.before: Blessed are you when people insult you, persecute you, and falsely say every kind of evil against you because of me.
verses.after: You are blessed when people insult you, persecute you, and falsely say every kind of evil against you because of me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed are you when people revile you and persecute you and utter all kinds of evil against you falsely on my account.

verses.rationale: Retains both joy commands and the prophetic continuity.
verses.before: Rejoice and be glad, because your reward is great in heaven. In the same way they persecuted the prophets who came before you.
verses.after: Rejoice and celebrate, because your reward in heaven is great. That is how they persecuted the prophets before you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Rejoice and be glad, for your reward is great in heaven, for in the same way they persecuted the prophets who were before you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the riddle and concrete fate without replacing salt with its supposed function.
verses.before: “You are the salt of the earth. But if salt becomes tasteless, how can its saltiness be restored? It is no longer good for anything except to be thrown outside and trampled underfoot.
verses.after: You are the salt of the earth. But if salt loses its saltiness, how can it be made salty again? It is good for nothing except to be thrown outside and trampled underfoot.
verses.tsw_comparator: You are the salt of the earth; but if salt has lost its taste, how can its saltiness be restored? It is no longer good for anything, but is thrown out and trampled under foot.

verses.rationale: Retains both light and elevated-city images.
verses.before: You are the light of the world. A city set on a hill cannot be hidden.
verses.after: You are the light of the world. A city set on a mountain cannot be hidden.
verses.tsw_comparator: You are the light of the world. A city built on a hill cannot be hidden.

verses.rationale: Preserves the household objects and universal household benefit.
verses.before: Neither do people light a lamp and put it under a basket. They put it on a lampstand, and it gives light to everyone in the house.
verses.after: No one lights a lamp and puts it under a grain basket. They put it on a lampstand, where it shines for everyone in the house.
verses.tsw_comparator: No one after lighting a lamp puts it under the basket, but on the lampstand, and it gives light to all in the house.

verses.rationale: Keeps the purpose directed to the Father rather than personal recognition.
verses.before: In the same way, let your light shine before people so that they may see your good works and glorify your Father in heaven.
verses.after: In the same way, let your light shine before people, so they may see your good works and glorify your Father in heaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the same way, let your light shine before others, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father in heaven.

verses.rationale: Retains both scriptural divisions and repeated abolish/fulfill contrast.
verses.before: “Do not think that I came to abolish the Law or the Prophets. I did not come to abolish but to fulfill.
verses.after: Do not think I came to abolish the Law or the Prophets. I came to fulfill them, not to abolish them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not think that I have come to abolish the law or the prophets; I have come not to abolish but to fulfill.

verses.rationale: Preserves both until clauses and the exactness image without specifying what everything must mean.
verses.before: Truly I tell you, until heaven and earth pass away, not one iota or one small stroke will pass from the Law until everything takes place.
verses.after: Truly I tell you: until heaven and earth pass away, not one smallest letter or pen stroke will pass from the Law until everything happens.
verses.tsw_comparator: For truly I tell you, until heaven and earth pass away, not one letter, not one stroke of a letter, will pass from the law until all is accomplished.

verses.rationale: Retains least/great and doing/teaching parallels.
verses.before: Therefore, whoever breaks one of the least of these commandments and teaches others to do the same will be called least in the kingdom of heaven. But whoever practices and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
verses.after: So whoever sets aside even one of these least commandments and teaches others to do the same will be called least in the kingdom of heaven. But whoever practices and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, whoever relaxes one of the least of these commandments and teaches others to do the same will be called least in the kingdom of heaven; but whoever does them and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.

verses.rationale: Keeps the strong negative and righteousness comparison without caricaturing the named groups.
verses.before: For I tell you that unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will certainly not enter the kingdom of heaven.
verses.after: For I tell you, unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will certainly not enter the kingdom of heaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I tell you, unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.

verses.rationale: Preserves address to earlier people and both quoted clauses.
verses.before: “You have heard that it was said to those of old, ‘Do not murder,’ and ‘Whoever murders will be liable to judgment.’
verses.after: You have heard that it was said to those of old, ‘Do not murder,’ and, ‘Whoever murders will answer to the court.’
verses.tsw_comparator: You have heard that it was said to those of ancient times, “You shall not murder”; and “whoever murders shall be liable to judgment.”

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned absence of without-cause, retains Raca/Gehenna with vocabulary support, and keeps the escalating judgments.
verses.before: But I tell you that everyone who is angry with a brother or sister will be liable to judgment; whoever says to a brother or sister, ‘Raca,’ will be liable to the council; and whoever says, ‘Fool!’ will be liable to the fire of Gehenna.
verses.after: But I tell you: anyone angry with a brother or sister will answer to the court. Whoever calls a brother or sister ‘Raca’ will answer to the council, and whoever says ‘Fool!’ will answer to fiery Gehenna.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I say to you that if you are angry with a brother or sister, you will be liable to judgment; and if you insult a brother or sister, you will be liable to the council; and if you say, “You fool,” you will be liable to the fire of Gehenna.

verses.rationale: Keeps the grievance as held by the other person and leaves the condition open.
verses.before: Therefore, if you are offering your gift at the altar and there remember that your brother or sister has something against you,
verses.after: So if you are bringing your gift to the altar and remember there that a brother or sister has something against you,
verses.tsw_comparator: So when you are offering your gift at the altar, if you remember that your brother or sister has something against you,

verses.rationale: Preserves the order of reconciliation before offering.
verses.before: leave your gift there before the altar. First go and be reconciled to your brother or sister; then come and offer your gift.
verses.after: leave your gift there before the altar. First go and be reconciled with that person; then come and offer your gift.
verses.tsw_comparator: leave your gift there before the altar and go; first be reconciled to your brother or sister, and then come and offer your gift.

verses.rationale: Keeps the legal progression and urgency of action on the way.
verses.before: Come to terms quickly with your accuser while you are still on the way to court, or your accuser may hand you over to the judge, the judge to the officer, and you may be thrown into prison.
verses.after: Come to terms with your accuser quickly while you are on the way together. Otherwise your accuser may hand you to the judge, the judge to the officer, and you will be thrown into prison.
verses.tsw_comparator: Come to terms quickly with your accuser while you are on the way to court with him, or your accuser may hand you over to the judge, and the judge to the guard, and you will be thrown into prison.

verses.rationale: Retains the smallest-debt image and ancient coin with vocabulary help.
verses.before: Truly I tell you, you will certainly not get out until you have paid the last penny.
verses.after: Truly I tell you: you will not get out until you have paid the last quadrans.
verses.tsw_comparator: Truly I tell you, you will never get out until you have paid the last penny.

verses.rationale: Retains the quotation without a later textual expansion.
verses.before: “You have heard that it was said, ‘Do not commit adultery.’
verses.after: You have heard that it was said, ‘Do not commit adultery.’
verses.tsw_comparator: You have heard that it was said, “You shall not commit adultery.”

verses.rationale: Keeps purposeful looking, specific male/woman relationship, and inner adultery; does not turn all noticing into the claim.
verses.before: But I tell you that everyone who looks at a woman in order to desire her has already committed adultery with her in the heart.
verses.after: But I tell you: anyone who looks at a woman in order to desire her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I say to you that everyone who looks at another with lust has already committed adultery with them in the heart.

verses.rationale: Preserves disturbing hyperbole, right eye, and part/whole contrast, with literary form noted.
verses.before: If your right eye causes you to stumble, tear it out and throw it away. It is better for you to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to be thrown into Gehenna.
verses.after: If your right eye causes you to stumble, tear it out and throw it away. It is better to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to be thrown into Gehenna.
verses.tsw_comparator: If your right eye causes you to stumble, tear it out and throw it away; it is better for you to lose one of your members than for your whole body to be thrown into Gehenna.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated hand version and source’s slightly different final verb.
verses.before: And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to go into Gehenna.
verses.after: And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away. It is better to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to go into Gehenna.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away; it is better for you to lose one of your members than for your whole body to go into Gehenna.

verses.rationale: Preserves the gendered legal setting and written certificate.
verses.before: “It was also said, ‘Whoever divorces his wife must give her a certificate of divorce.’
verses.after: It was also said, ‘Whoever divorces his wife must give her a certificate of divorce.’
verses.tsw_comparator: It was also said, “Whoever divorces his wife, let him give her a certificate of divorce.”

verses.rationale: Retains exception, causative responsibility, and passive involvement, with porneia and syntax explained briefly rather than used as pastoral advice.
verses.before: But I tell you that everyone who divorces his wife, except on account of sexual immorality, causes her to be subjected to adultery; and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
verses.after: But I tell you: anyone who divorces his wife, except on grounds of sexual immorality, causes her to be involved in adultery, and anyone who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I say to you that anyone who divorces his wife, except on the ground of unfaithfulness, causes her to commit adultery; and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.

verses.rationale: Keeps both prohibitory and positive oath obligations.
verses.before: “Again, you have heard that it was said to those of old, ‘Do not break your oath, but fulfill your oaths to the Lord.’
verses.after: Again, you have heard that it was said to those of old, ‘Do not swear falsely, but fulfill your oaths to the Lord.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Again, you have heard that it was said to those of ancient times, “You shall not swear falsely, but carry out the vows you have made to the Lord.”

verses.rationale: Retains comprehensive prohibition and first supporting image.
verses.before: But I tell you: do not swear at all—neither by heaven, because it is God's throne;
verses.after: But I tell you not to swear at all: neither by heaven, because it is God’s throne,
verses.tsw_comparator: But I say to you, do not swear at all, either by heaven, for it is the throne of God,

verses.rationale: Preserves both further referents and reasons.
verses.before: nor by the earth, because it is his footstool; nor by Jerusalem, because it is the city of the great King.
verses.after: nor by earth, because it is his footstool, nor by Jerusalem, because it is the city of the great King.
verses.tsw_comparator: or by the earth, for it is the footstool of God, or by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.

verses.rationale: Keeps the bodily example and exact single-hair limit.
verses.before: Do not swear by your head, because you cannot make one hair white or black.
verses.after: Do not swear by your own head either, because you cannot make a single hair white or black.
verses.tsw_comparator: And do not swear by your head, for you cannot make one hair white or black.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated yes/no and leaves evil/evil-one ambiguity noted.
verses.before: Let your word be simply ‘Yes, yes’ or ‘No, no.’ Anything more than this comes from evil.
verses.after: Let your words be ‘Yes, yes’ or ‘No, no.’ Anything beyond this comes from evil.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let your word be “Yes, Yes” or “No, No”; anything more than this comes from the evil one.

verses.rationale: Retains the familiar legal formula rather than changing it for novelty.
verses.before: “You have heard that it was said, ‘Eye for eye and tooth for tooth.’
verses.after: You have heard that it was said, ‘An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.’
verses.tsw_comparator: You have heard that it was said, “An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the force of nonresistance and specific right cheek without inserting an interpretive limit.
verses.before: But I tell you: do not retaliate against an evildoer. Instead, if anyone strikes you on the right cheek, turn the other to them also.
verses.after: But I tell you not to resist the wrongdoer. If someone strikes your right cheek, turn the other to him too.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I say to you, do not resist an evildoer. But if anyone strikes you on the right cheek, turn the other also;

verses.rationale: Preserves legal setting and distinct inner/outer garments.
verses.before: If anyone wants to sue you and take your tunic, let them have your cloak as well.
verses.after: If someone wants to sue you for your tunic, let him have your cloak as well.
verses.tsw_comparator: and if anyone wants to sue you and take your coat, give your cloak as well;

verses.rationale: Keeps coercion and exact one/two contrast.
verses.before: If anyone forces you to go one mile, go with them two.
verses.after: If someone forces you to go one mile, go two with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: and if anyone forces you to go one mile, go also the second mile.

verses.rationale: Retains separate giving and lending commands.
verses.before: Give to the one who asks you, and do not turn away from the one who wants to borrow from you.
verses.after: Give to the one who asks you, and do not turn away someone who wants to borrow from you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Give to everyone who begs from you, and do not refuse anyone who wants to borrow from you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the cited saying without falsely assigning the entire phrase to Torah in a note.
verses.before: “You have heard that it was said, ‘Love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’
verses.after: You have heard that it was said, ‘Love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’
verses.tsw_comparator: You have heard that it was said, “You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.”

verses.rationale: Follows the shorter pinned text and keeps both enemy-love and prayer.
verses.before: But I tell you: love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,
verses.after: But I tell you: love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,
verses.tsw_comparator: But I say to you, love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,

verses.rationale: Preserves divine-family purpose and both weather gifts across moral contrasts.
verses.before: so that you may be children of your Father in heaven. For he makes his sun rise on evil and good people and sends rain on righteous and unrighteous people.
verses.after: so you may be children of your Father in heaven. He makes his sun rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that you may be children of your Father in heaven; for God makes the sun rise on the evil and on the good, and sends rain on the righteous and on the unrighteous.

verses.rationale: Keeps the rhetorical question and named comparison group.
verses.before: If you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even tax collectors do the same?
verses.after: If you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even tax collectors do the same?
verses.tsw_comparator: For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the same?

verses.rationale: Preserves greeting, exclusive circle, and nations without importing a new insult. Renders ethnikoí as Gentiles, identifying non-Jewish people rather than political nations.
verses.before: And if you greet only your own people, what are you doing beyond others? Do not even the Gentiles do the same?
verses.after: And if you greet only your own brothers and sisters, what more are you doing? Do not even Gentiles do the same?
verses.tsw_comparator: And if you greet only your brothers and sisters, what more are you doing than others? Do not even the Gentiles do the same?

verses.rationale: Keeps the telos/wholeness force in context, with perfect as a lexical alternative noted.
verses.before: Therefore, be complete, as your heavenly Father is complete.
verses.after: So be complete, as your heavenly Father is complete.
verses.tsw_comparator: Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect.

verses.rationale: Follows pinned righteousness and preserves the motive qualification linking the examples.
verses.before: “Be careful not to practice your righteousness in front of people in order to be seen by them. Otherwise you have no reward from your Father in heaven.
verses.after: Be careful not to practice your righteousness before people in order to be seen by them. Otherwise you have no reward from your Father in heaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: Take care not to do your righteousness in front of others to be seen by them. If you do, you have no reward from your Father in the heavens.

verses.rationale: Keeps almsgiving concrete, the trumpet image, and full-payment refrain.
verses.before: So whenever you give to the poor, do not sound a trumpet before you as hypocrites do in the synagogues and streets so that people will honor them. Truly I tell you, they have received their reward in full.
verses.after: So when you give to the poor, do not sound a trumpet ahead of you, as hypocrites do in synagogues and streets to win people’s praise. Truly I tell you: they have received their reward in full.
verses.tsw_comparator: So whenever you give alms, do not blow a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, so that they may be honored by others. Truly I tell you, they have received their reward in full.

verses.rationale: Preserves the impossible secrecy image rather than converting it to advice about bookkeeping.
verses.before: But when you give to the poor, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,
verses.after: But when you give to the poor, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,
verses.tsw_comparator: But when you give alms, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,

verses.rationale: Keeps the secret/seeing contrast and no added openly.
verses.before: so that your giving may be in secret. And your Father, who sees in secret, will reward you.
verses.after: so your giving may be in secret. Your Father, who sees in secret, will repay you.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that your alms may be in secret; and your Father, who sees in secret, will repay you.

verses.rationale: Retains visibility motive and repeats the reward refrain exactly.
verses.before: “And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites, because they love to stand and pray in synagogues and on street corners so that people will see them. Truly I tell you, they have received their reward in full.
verses.after: When you pray, do not be like the hypocrites. They love to stand praying in synagogues and on street corners so people will see them. Truly I tell you: they have received their reward in full.
verses.tsw_comparator: And whenever you pray, do not be like the hypocrites; for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and at the corners of the streets, so that they may be seen by others. Truly I tell you, they have received their reward in full.

verses.rationale: Preserves private-room sequence and repeated secret language.
verses.before: But when you pray, go into your private room, shut the door, and pray to your Father who is in secret. And your Father, who sees in secret, will reward you.
verses.after: But when you pray, go into your inner room, shut the door, and pray to your Father who is in secret. Your Father, who sees in secret, will repay you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when you pray, go into your room, shut the door, and pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father, who sees in secret, will repay you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the critique of speech and presumed efficacy without treating all repeated prayer as condemned. Renders ethnikoí as Gentiles, identifying non-Jewish people rather than political nations.
verses.before: When you pray, do not pile up empty words as the Gentiles do, because they think they will be heard because of their many words.
verses.after: When you pray, do not babble like Gentiles. They think they will be heard because of their many words.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when you pray, do not heap up empty phrases as the Gentiles do; for they think they will be heard for their many words.

verses.rationale: Retains divine knowledge before asking without deleting the call to prayer.
verses.before: Do not be like them, because your Father knows what you need before you ask him.
verses.after: Do not be like them. Your Father knows what you need before you ask him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask him.

verses.rationale: Keeps plural our and passive sanctification as a petition.
verses.before: “Therefore pray like this: Our Father in heaven, may your name be made holy.
verses.after: Pray like this: ‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be held holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pray then in this way: Our Father in the heavens, hallowed be your name.

verses.rationale: Preserves three parallel petitions and earthly realization.
verses.before: May your kingdom come. May your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.
verses.after: May your kingdom come. May your will be done on earth as in heaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your kingdom come. Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.

verses.rationale: Chooses needed bread for epiousios, with daily/coming-day alternatives noted.
verses.before: Give us today our daily bread.
verses.after: Give us today the bread we need.
verses.tsw_comparator: Give us this day our daily bread.

verses.rationale: Retains debts metaphor and pinned past have-forgiven.
verses.before: And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.
verses.after: Forgive us our debts, as we too have forgiven our debtors.
verses.tsw_comparator: And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.

verses.rationale: Keeps the difficult divine-agency petition, evil/evil-one ambiguity, and absence of later doxology.
verses.before: And do not bring us into testing, but rescue us from the evil one.
verses.after: Do not bring us into testing, but rescue us from evil.’
verses.tsw_comparator: And do not bring us into testing, but deliver us from the evil one.

verses.rationale: Preserves the conditional reciprocity and transition from debts to offenses.
verses.before: “For if you forgive people their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
verses.after: For if you forgive people their offenses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
verses.tsw_comparator: For if you forgive others their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you;

verses.rationale: Keeps the negative counterpart without adding an unstated object to the first clause.
verses.before: But if you do not forgive people, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
verses.after: But if you do not forgive people, your Father will not forgive your offenses.
verses.tsw_comparator: but if you do not forgive others their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.

verses.rationale: Preserves appearance motive and the third exact reward refrain.
verses.before: “Whenever you fast, do not become gloomy like the hypocrites. They neglect their appearance so that their fasting will be visible to people. Truly I tell you, they have received their reward in full.
verses.after: When you fast, do not look gloomy like the hypocrites. They disfigure their faces so people will notice they are fasting. Truly I tell you: they have received their reward in full.
verses.tsw_comparator: And whenever you fast, do not look gloomy like the hypocrites; for they disfigure their faces so as to show others that they are fasting. Truly I tell you, they have received their reward in full.

verses.rationale: Keeps the ordinary grooming actions rather than a modern equivalent.
verses.before: But when you fast, put oil on your head and wash your face,
verses.after: But when you fast, put oil on your head and wash your face,
verses.tsw_comparator: But when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face,

verses.rationale: Retains the visibility contrast and repeated private reward wording.
verses.before: so that your fasting will not be seen by people but by your Father who is in secret. And your Father, who sees in secret, will reward you.
verses.after: so your fasting is seen by your Father who is in secret, not by people. Your Father, who sees in secret, will repay you.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that your fasting may be seen not by others but by your Father who is in secret; and your Father, who sees in secret, will repay you.

verses.rationale: Keeps moth, consuming decay, and burglary images.
verses.before: “Do not store up treasures for yourselves on earth, where moth and decay destroy and thieves break in and steal.
verses.after: Do not store up treasures for yourselves on earth, where moth and decay destroy and thieves break in and steal.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust consume and where thieves break in and steal;

verses.rationale: Mirrors the preceding sentence to retain its contrast and repetition.
verses.before: Instead, store up treasures for yourselves in heaven, where neither moth nor decay destroys and thieves do not break in and steal.
verses.after: Store up treasures for yourselves in heaven, where neither moth nor decay destroys and thieves do not break in or steal.
verses.tsw_comparator: but store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust consumes and where thieves do not break in and steal.

verses.rationale: Retains singular your and the familiar heart/treasure relation.
verses.before: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
verses.after: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be too.
verses.tsw_comparator: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.

verses.rationale: Keeps eye/lamp and whole-body light; single/generous nuances noted.
verses.before: “The eye is the lamp of the body. So if your eye is healthy, your whole body will be full of light.
verses.after: The eye is the body’s lamp. If your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light.
verses.tsw_comparator: The eye is the lamp of the body. So if your eye is single, your whole body will be full of light;

verses.rationale: Preserves the paradox and exclamation without reducing it to eyesight advice.
verses.before: But if your eye is bad, your whole body will be full of darkness. Therefore, if the light within you is darkness, how great is that darkness!
verses.after: But if your eye is bad, your whole body will be dark. If the light within you is darkness, how great that darkness is!
verses.tsw_comparator: but if your eye is evil, your whole body will be full of darkness. If then the light in you is darkness, how great is that darkness!

verses.rationale: Keeps slavery-service, opposed allegiances, and mammon as wealth with vocabulary support.
verses.before: “No one can serve two masters, because either you will hate one and love the other, or you will be devoted to one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and wealth.
verses.after: No one can serve two masters. You will hate one and love the other, or be devoted to one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and wealth.
verses.tsw_comparator: No one can serve two masters; for either you will hate the one and love the other, or you will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and wealth.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned shorter first list and keeps the life/body comparison.
verses.before: “Therefore I tell you: do not be anxious about your life—what you will eat or drink—or about your body—what you will wear. Is not life more than food and the body more than clothing?
verses.after: That is why I tell you: do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear. Is life not more than food, and the body more than clothing?
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I tell you, do not be anxious about your life, what you will eat or what you will drink, or about your body, what you will wear. Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothing?

verses.rationale: Preserves all three agricultural absences and rhetorical comparison.
verses.before: Look at the birds of the sky. They do not sow or reap or gather into barns, yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not worth much more than they are?
verses.after: Look at the birds of heaven. They neither sow nor reap nor gather into storehouses, yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not worth more than they are?
verses.tsw_comparator: Look at the birds of the air; they neither sow nor reap nor gather into barns, and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not of more value than they?

verses.rationale: Retains the deliberately mixed measurement image and notes stature/lifespan ambiguity.
verses.before: And which of you by being anxious can add a single cubit to your span of life?
verses.after: Which of you can add a single cubit to your lifespan by worrying?
verses.tsw_comparator: And which of you by being anxious can add a single hour to your life?

verses.rationale: Keeps the observation invitation and both absent forms of work.
verses.before: Why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow. They do not labor or spin,
verses.after: And why worry about clothing? Consider how the field’s lilies grow. They neither labor nor spin,
verses.tsw_comparator: And why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they neither toil nor spin,

verses.rationale: Retains specific royal comparison and single flower.
verses.before: yet I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.
verses.after: yet I tell you, even Solomon in all his glory was not clothed like one of them.
verses.tsw_comparator: yet I tell you, even Solomon in all his glory was not clothed like one of these.

verses.rationale: Preserves ephemeral fuel, divine provision, and direct faith rebuke.
verses.before: If God clothes the grass of the field this way—alive today and tomorrow thrown into the oven—will he not much more clothe you, you of little trust?
verses.after: If God clothes the field’s grass this way, though it is here today and thrown into the oven tomorrow, will he not clothe you much more, you of little faith?
verses.tsw_comparator: But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which is alive today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, will he not much more clothe you—you of little faith?

verses.rationale: Retains all three practical questions in their repeated form.
verses.before: Therefore do not be anxious, saying, ‘What will we eat?’ or ‘What will we drink?’ or ‘What will we wear?’
verses.after: So do not worry, asking, ‘What will we eat?’ or ‘What will we drink?’ or ‘What will we wear?’
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore do not be anxious, saying, “What shall we eat?” or “What shall we drink?” or “What shall we wear?”

verses.rationale: Keeps nations, all twice, and the Father’s knowledge.
verses.before: The Gentiles pursue all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them.
verses.after: The nations seek all these things, and your heavenly Father knows you need them all.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the Gentiles seek all these things; and your heavenly Father knows that you need them all.

verses.rationale: Follows pinned absence of of-God after kingdom and preserves righteousness and priority.
verses.before: But seek first God's kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well.
verses.after: Seek first the kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well.
verses.tsw_comparator: But seek first his kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you.

verses.rationale: Retains personified tomorrow and the limited daily horizon.
verses.before: Therefore do not be anxious about tomorrow, because tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Each day has enough trouble of its own.
verses.after: So do not worry about tomorrow. Tomorrow will worry about itself. Each day has enough trouble of its own.
verses.tsw_comparator: So do not be anxious about tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Today’s trouble is enough for today.

verses.rationale: Keeps the uncompromising command and passive consequence.
verses.before: “Do not judge, so that you will not be judged.
verses.after: Do not judge, so that you will not be judged.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Do not judge, so that you may not be judged.

verses.rationale: Preserves the two reciprocal images and passive agency.
verses.before: For with the judgment you use, you will be judged, and with the measure you use, it will be measured to you.
verses.after: For the judgment you give will be given to you, and the measure you use will be used for you.
verses.tsw_comparator: For with the judgment you pronounce you will be judged, and with the measure you use it will be measured to you.

verses.rationale: Retains the absurd scale contrast and inclusive fellow-member referent.
verses.before: Why do you look at the speck in your brother's or sister's eye but do not notice the beam in your own eye?
verses.after: Why do you notice the speck in your brother’s or sister’s eye but fail to consider the beam in your own?
verses.tsw_comparator: Why do you see the speck that is in your brother’s eye, but do not notice the log that is in your own eye?

verses.rationale: Keeps quoted offer and self-contradictory situation.
verses.before: Or how can you say, ‘Let me take the speck out of your eye,’ when there is a beam in your own?
verses.after: How can you say, ‘Let me remove the speck from your eye,’ when there is a beam in your own eye?
verses.tsw_comparator: Or how can you say to your brother, ‘Let me take the speck out of your eye,’ when there is the log in your own eye?

verses.rationale: Preserves first/then order and the eventual ability to help.
verses.before: Hypocrite! First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your brother's or sister's eye.
verses.after: Hypocrite! First remove the beam from your own eye. Then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s or sister’s eye.
verses.tsw_comparator: You hypocrite, first take the log out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your brother’s eye.

verses.rationale: Retains animals, precious objects, and violent reversal without assigning modern groups to them.
verses.before: “Do not give what is holy to dogs, and do not throw your pearls before pigs, or they may trample them under their feet and turn and tear you apart.
verses.after: Do not give what is holy to dogs or throw your pearls before pigs. They may trample them underfoot, then turn and tear you apart.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not give what is holy to dogs, and do not throw your pearls before pigs, lest they trample them underfoot and turn to attack you.

verses.rationale: Preserves the three parallel commands and promises.
verses.before: “Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.
verses.after: Ask, and it will be given to you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and the door will be opened to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.

verses.rationale: Retains the complete repetition in indicative form.
verses.before: For everyone who asks receives, the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks the door will be opened.
verses.after: For everyone who asks receives; the one who seeks finds; and to the one who knocks, the door will be opened.
verses.tsw_comparator: For everyone who asks receives, and the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened.

verses.rationale: Keeps father/son and the food/stone contrast.
verses.before: Or which of you, if your child asks for bread, will give a stone?
verses.after: Who among you would give his son a stone when he asks for bread?
verses.tsw_comparator: Or which one of you, if his son asks him for bread, will give him a stone?

verses.rationale: Preserves the parallel question and specific animals.
verses.before: Or if the child asks for a fish, will give a snake?
verses.after: Or give him a snake when he asks for a fish?
verses.tsw_comparator: Or if he asks for a fish, will give him a serpent?

verses.rationale: Retains the troubling evil assessment and greater divine generosity without importing Luke’s Spirit wording.
verses.before: If you, though you are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask him!
verses.after: If you, evil as you are, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask him!
verses.tsw_comparator: If you then, who are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask him.

verses.rationale: Keeps comprehensive scope, active obligation, and scriptural summary.
verses.before: Therefore, in everything, do to others whatever you want them to do to you. For this is the Law and the Prophets.
verses.after: So in everything, do for others what you want them to do for you. This is the Law and the Prophets.
verses.tsw_comparator: So whatever you wish that others would do to you, do also to them, for this is the Law and the Prophets.

verses.rationale: Preserves both gate and road and the many travelers.
verses.before: “Enter through the narrow gate. For the gate is wide and the road broad that leads to destruction, and many enter through it.
verses.after: Enter through the narrow gate. The gate is wide and the road spacious that leads to destruction, and many enter through it.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Enter through the narrow gate. For the gate is wide and the way is broad that leads to destruction, and many enter through it.

verses.rationale: Keeps the constrained road and few without turning the image into statistics.
verses.before: But the gate is narrow and the road constricted that leads to life, and few find it.
verses.after: But the gate is narrow and the road constricted that leads to life, and few find it.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the gate is narrow and the way is constrained that leads to life, and few find it.

verses.rationale: Retains disguise, inward reality, and predatory force.
verses.before: “Watch out for false prophets. They come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravenous wolves.
verses.after: Watch out for false prophets. They come to you dressed as sheep, but inwardly they are ravenous wolves.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing but inwardly are ravenous wolves.

verses.rationale: Keeps the fruit criterion and both botanical questions.
verses.before: You will recognize them by their fruits. Are grapes gathered from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?
verses.after: You will recognize them by their fruit. Are grapes gathered from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?
verses.tsw_comparator: You will know them by their fruits. Are grapes gathered from thorns, or figs from thistles?

verses.rationale: Retains tree/fruit relation and rotten rather than merely different.
verses.before: In the same way, every good tree produces good fruit, but a bad tree produces bad fruit.
verses.after: In the same way, every good tree produces good fruit, while a rotten tree produces bad fruit.
verses.tsw_comparator: So every good tree bears good fruit, but the bad tree bears bad fruit.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated impossibility and reverse parallel.

verses.after: A good tree cannot produce bad fruit, nor can a rotten tree produce good fruit.
verses.tsw_comparator: A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, nor can a bad tree bear good fruit.

verses.rationale: Matches the recurring judgment wording from chapter three.
verses.before: Every tree that does not produce good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
verses.after: Every tree that fails to produce good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.

verses.rationale: Retains the closing repetition of the criterion.
verses.before: So then, you will recognize them by their fruits.
verses.after: So you will recognize them by their fruit.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus you will know them by their fruits.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated Lord and the contrast between speech and doing.

verses.rationale: Keeps all three claims and three in-your-name repetitions.
verses.before: Many will say to me on that day, ‘Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, cast out demons in your name, and do many works of power in your name?’
verses.after: Many will say to me on that day, ‘Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, drive out demons in your name, and do many mighty works in your name?’
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day many will say to me, ‘Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, and cast out demons in your name, and do many mighty works in your name?’

verses.rationale: Preserves never, personal rejection, and lawlessness without softening it.

verses.after: Then I will tell them plainly, ‘I never knew you. Depart from me, you workers of lawlessness!’
verses.tsw_comparator: And then I will declare to them, ‘I never knew you; depart from me, you workers of lawlessness.’

verses.rationale: Keeps hearing/doing and the wise builder with concrete foundation.
verses.before: “Therefore everyone who hears these words of mine and does them will be like a wise man who built his house on rock.
verses.after: So everyone who hears these words of mine and does them will be like a wise man who built his house on rock.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Everyone then who hears these words of mine and does them will be like a wise man who built his house on the rock.

verses.rationale: Preserves all three pressures and the stated reason for survival.
verses.before: The rain fell, the floods came, and the winds blew and beat against that house, but it did not fall, because its foundation had been laid on rock.
verses.after: The rain came down, the rivers rose, and the winds blew and beat against that house. But it did not fall, because its foundation was on rock.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the rain fell, and the floods came, and the winds blew and beat against that house, but it did not fall, because it had been founded on the rock.

verses.rationale: Mirrors the prior builder while retaining the decisive failure to act.
verses.before: And everyone who hears these words of mine and does not do them will be like a foolish man who built his house on sand.
verses.after: Everyone who hears these words of mine and does not do them will be like a foolish man who built his house on sand.
verses.tsw_comparator: And everyone who hears these words of mine and does not do them will be like a foolish man who built his house on the sand.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated storm sequence and emphatic collapse.
verses.before: The rain fell, the floods came, and the winds blew and struck that house, and it fell—and its fall was great.”
verses.after: The rain came down, the rivers rose, and the winds blew and struck that house. It fell, and its fall was great.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And the rain fell, and the floods came, and the winds blew and struck that house, and it fell—and great was its fall.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the discourse-ending formula and crowd response.
verses.before: When Jesus finished these words, the crowds were astonished at his teaching,
verses.after: When Jesus finished saying these things, the crowds were astonished at his teaching,

verses.rationale: Retains the narrator’s explanation and specific comparison without broad claims about Judaism.
verses.before: because he was teaching them as one who had authority, and not like their scribes.
verses.after: because he taught them as someone with authority, unlike their scribes.
verses.tsw_comparator: for he was teaching them as one having authority, and not as their scribes.

verses.rationale: Names the returning subject and preserves the movement from teaching to encounter.
verses.before: When Jesus came down from the mountain, large crowds followed him.
verses.after: When Jesus came down from the mountain, large crowds followed him.
verses.tsw_comparator: When he came down from the mountain, great crowds followed him.

verses.rationale: Keeps willingness distinct from ability and avoids a modern diagnosis for lepros.

verses.after: A man with a skin disease came up, bowed before him, and said, “Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And behold, a leper came near and knelt before him, saying, “Lord, if you will, you are able to make me clean.”

verses.before: Jesus reached out his hand, touched him, and said, “I am willing. Be made clean.” Immediately he was cleansed of the disease.
verses.after: Jesus reached out and touched him. “I am willing,” he said. “Be clean.” At once the man’s skin disease was cleansed.
verses.tsw_comparator: And stretching out his hand, he touched him, saying, “I will; be made clean.” And immediately his leprosy was cleansed.

verses.rationale: Preserves the prohibition and ritual testimony without specifying its disputed audience.

verses.after: Then Jesus told him, “See that you tell no one. Go, show yourself to the priest, and offer the gift Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Jesus said to him, “See that you say nothing to anyone; but go, show yourself to the priest and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony to them.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the military title and lets the plea continue across the label.

verses.after: As Jesus entered Capernaum, a centurion approached him, pleading,
verses.tsw_comparator: When he entered Capernaum, a centurion came to him, appealing to him,

verses.rationale: Renders pais as servant in context while preserving paralysis and severe suffering.

verses.after: “Lord, my servant is lying at home, paralyzed and suffering terribly.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and saying, “Lord, my servant is lying at home paralyzed, terribly afflicted.”

verses.rationale: Retains the emphatic personal offer; the possible question belongs in a note.
verses.before: Jesus said to him, “I will come and heal him.”
verses.after: Jesus said to him, “I will come and heal him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to him, “I will come and heal him.”

verses.rationale: Preserves roof imagery and confidence in a spoken command.

verses.after: The centurion answered, “Lord, I am not worthy to have you come under my roof. Just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the centurion answered, “Lord, I am not worthy that you should come under my roof, but only speak a word, and my servant will be healed.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes doulos from pais and preserves each command and response.

verses.after: I too am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I tell one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; another, ‘Come,’ and he comes; and my slave, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For I also am a man under authority, with soldiers under me; and I say to one, ‘Go,’ and he goes, and to another, ‘Come,’ and he comes, and to my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the source’s comparative claim without adding universal ethnic judgment.

verses.after: When Jesus heard this, he was amazed. He told those following him, “Truly I tell you, I have found no one in Israel with faith like this.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Jesus heard this, he marveled and said to those who followed him, “Truly I tell you, with no one in Israel have I found such faith.

verses.rationale: Makes reclining intelligible as a feast while retaining named ancestors and directions.
verses.before: I tell you that many will come from east and west and will recline at the table with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven,
verses.after: And I tell you, many will come from east and west and take their places at the feast with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.

verses.rationale: Preserves the direct address and precise correspondence in time.
verses.before: Then Jesus said to the centurion, “Go. Let it happen for you as you trusted.” And the servant was healed at that hour.
verses.after: Then Jesus told the centurion, “Go. Let it happen for you as you have believed.” And the servant was healed at that very hour.
verses.tsw_comparator: And to the centurion Jesus said, “Go; let it be done for you as you have believed.” And the servant was healed at that very hour.

verses.rationale: Makes the relationship explicit without adding a household history.
verses.before: When Jesus came into Peter's house, he saw Peter's mother-in-law lying in bed with a fever.
verses.after: Jesus went into Peter’s house and saw Peter’s mother-in-law lying sick with a fever.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when Jesus entered Peter’s house, he saw his mother-in-law lying sick with a fever.

verses.rationale: Retains female agency and the singular recipient of service.
verses.before: He touched her hand, and the fever left her. She got up and began serving him.
verses.after: He touched her hand, and the fever left her. She got up and began serving him.
verses.tsw_comparator: He touched her hand, and the fever left her, and she rose and began to serve him.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes spirits from illness and retains comprehensive healing.
verses.before: When evening came, people brought to him many who were oppressed by demons. He cast out the spirits with a word and healed everyone who was sick,
verses.after: That evening, people brought him many who were possessed by demons. He drove out the spirits with a word and healed everyone who was ill.
verses.tsw_comparator: That evening they brought to him many who were oppressed by demons, and he cast out the spirits with a word and healed all who were sick.

verses.rationale: Keeps Matthew’s bodily wording and shapes the quotation as poetry within its verse.
verses.before: so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled: “He took our weaknesses and carried our diseases.”
verses.after: This fulfilled what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah: “He took our weaknesses and carried our diseases.”
verses.tsw_comparator: This was to fulfill what was spoken by the prophet Isaiah: “He took our illnesses and bore our diseases.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the source’s plural crowds and unspecified destination shore.
verses.before: When Jesus saw a crowd around him, he gave orders to go to the other side.
verses.after: When Jesus saw the large crowds around him, he gave orders to cross to the other side.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now when Jesus saw a crowd around him, he gave orders to go over to the other side.

verses.rationale: Retains the trained role and the unqualified offer.
verses.before: A scribe came and said to him, “Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go.”
verses.after: A scribe came up and said, “Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And a scribe came and said to him, “Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the title and complete animal contrast rather than explaining away the image.
verses.before: Jesus told him, “Foxes have dens and birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”
verses.after: Jesus answered him, “Foxes have dens, and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Jesus said to him, “Foxes have holes, and birds of the air have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”

verses.rationale: Preserves first and the actual request without inventing circumstances of death.

verses.after: Another of the disciples said to him, “Lord, first let me go and bury my father.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Another of the disciples said to him, “Lord, let me first go and bury my father.”

verses.rationale: Retains the disturbing double use of dead without resolving its metaphor in the text.
verses.before: But Jesus said to him, “Follow me, and let the dead bury their own dead.”
verses.after: But Jesus told him, “Follow me, and let the dead bury their own dead.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Jesus said to him, “Follow me, and leave the dead to bury their own dead.”

verses.rationale: Keeps following visible as both action and narrative theme.
verses.before: Jesus got into the boat, and his disciples followed him.
verses.after: Jesus got into a boat, and his disciples followed him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when he got into the boat, his disciples followed him.

verses.rationale: Renders seismos strongly without deciding that an earthquake caused the waves.
verses.before: Suddenly a great storm arose on the sea, so that the boat was being covered by the waves. But Jesus was sleeping.
verses.after: Suddenly a violent disturbance swept over the sea, and waves were covering the boat. But Jesus was asleep.
verses.tsw_comparator: And behold, there arose a great storm on the sea, so that the boat was being covered by the waves; but he was asleep.

verses.rationale: Keeps the urgent salvation plea and immediate danger in natural speech.
verses.before: They came and woke him, saying, “Lord, save us! We are perishing!”
verses.after: They went to him and woke him. “Lord, save us!” they said. “We’re going to die!”
verses.tsw_comparator: And they went and woke him, saying, “Lord, save us; we are perishing.”

verses.rationale: Retains little faith, rebuke, and the great disturbance/great calm contrast.
verses.before: He said to them, “Why are you afraid, you of little trust?” Then he got up, rebuked the winds and the sea, and there was a great calm.
verses.after: He said to them, “Why are you so afraid, you of little faith?” Then he got up and rebuked the winds and the sea, and a great calm came over it.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to them, “Why are you afraid, you of little faith?” Then he rose and rebuked the winds and the sea, and there was a great calm.

verses.rationale: Preserves their unresolved question and the scope of obedience.
verses.before: The men were amazed and said, “What kind of man is this? Even the winds and the sea obey him!”
verses.after: The men were amazed. “What kind of man is this,” they said, “that even the winds and the sea obey him?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And the men marveled, saying, “What sort of man is this, that even winds and sea obey him?”

verses.rationale: Retains two men and the pinned place name without harmonizing other accounts.
