verses.after: When he reached the other side, in the region of the Gadarenes, two demon-possessed men came out from the tombs to meet him. They were so violent that no one could pass along that road.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when he came to the other side, to the country of the Gadarenes, two men possessed by demons met him, coming out of the tombs, so fierce that no one could pass that way.

verses.rationale: Preserves title, antagonistic idiom, and premature judgment question.
verses.before: And look—they cried out, “What do you want with us, Son of God? Have you come here to torment us before the appointed time?”
verses.after: They shouted, “What have you to do with us, Son of God? Have you come here to torment us before the appointed time?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And behold, they cried out, “What have you to do with us, Son of God? Have you come here to torment us before the appointed time?”

verses.rationale: Keeps distance and herd size without locating an unmentioned owner.
verses.before: Some distance away, a large herd of pigs was feeding.
verses.after: A large herd of pigs was feeding some distance away.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now a herd of many pigs was feeding at some distance from them.

verses.rationale: Retains the conditional request and its actual destination.
verses.before: The demons begged him, “If you cast us out, send us into the herd of pigs.”
verses.after: The demons begged him, “If you drive us out, send us into the herd of pigs.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And the demons begged him, saying, “If you cast us out, send us away into the herd of pigs.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the lethal outcome and every stage without softening the loss.
verses.before: He said to them, “Go.” They came out and went into the pigs, and the whole herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea and died in the water.

verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to them, “Go.” So they came out and went into the pigs, and behold, the whole herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea and drowned in the waters.

verses.rationale: Makes the compressed report intelligible without supplying unreported reactions.
verses.before: The herders fled, went into the city, and reported everything, including what had happened to the demonized men.
verses.after: The herders ran away. They went into the town and reported everything, including what had happened to the demon-possessed men.
verses.tsw_comparator: The herdsmen fled, and going into the city they told everything, especially what had happened to the demon-possessed men.

verses.rationale: Keeps the collective response and unexpected request to depart.
verses.before: Then the whole city went out to meet Jesus. When they saw him, they begged him to leave their region.
verses.after: The whole town came out to meet Jesus. When they saw him, they begged him to leave their region.
verses.tsw_comparator: And behold, all the city came out to meet Jesus, and when they saw him, they begged him to depart from their region.

verses.rationale: Retains own town without inserting its inferred name.
verses.before: Jesus got into a boat, crossed over, and came to his own town.
verses.after: Jesus got into a boat, crossed over, and came to his own town.
verses.tsw_comparator: And getting into a boat, he crossed over and came to his own city.

verses.rationale: Keeps their plural faith and the affectionate singular address.

verses.after: Some people brought him a paralyzed man lying on a mat. When Jesus saw their faith, he told the man, “Take courage, child. Your sins are forgiven.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And behold, they brought to him a paralytic lying on a bed. And when Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, “Take courage, child; your sins are forgiven.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the inward accusation without endorsing it as narrator.
verses.before: Then some of the scribes said to themselves, “This man is blaspheming.”
verses.after: Some of the scribes said to themselves, “This man is blaspheming.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And behold, some of the scribes said to themselves, “This man blasphemes.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the heart image and explicit moral challenge.

verses.after: Jesus knew what they were thinking. “Why are you thinking evil in your hearts?” he asked.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Jesus, knowing their thoughts, said, “Why do you think evil in your hearts?

verses.rationale: Retains the comparison between sayings, not a claim that either act is easy.

verses.after: “Which is easier: to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk’?
verses.tsw_comparator: For which is easier, to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Rise and walk’?

verses.rationale: Preserves the interrupted sentence and changed addressee.
verses.before: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—then he said to the paralytic—“Get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”
verses.after: But so that you may know the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—then he said to the paralyzed man, “Get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he then said to the paralytic—“Rise, take up your bed, and go to your house.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the concise enacted response without embellishment.
verses.before: The man got up and went home.
verses.after: The man got up and went home.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he rose and went to his house.

verses.rationale: Follows fear and plural humans rather than harmonizing to amazement or Jesus alone.
verses.before: When the crowds saw this, they were afraid and glorified God, who had given such authority to human beings.
verses.after: When the crowds saw this, they were afraid and glorified God, who had given such authority to human beings.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when the crowds saw it, they were afraid, and they glorified God, who had given such authority to men.

verses.rationale: Keeps the call-response pattern and names the actor for clarity.

verses.after: As Jesus went on from there, he saw a man named Matthew sitting at the tax booth. “Follow me,” he told him. Matthew got up and followed him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And as Jesus passed on from there, he saw a man called Matthew sitting at the tax booth, and he said to him, “Follow me.” And he rose and followed him.

verses.rationale: Retains reclining and avoids assigning ownership to the unspecified house.
verses.before: While Jesus was reclining at the table in the house, many tax collectors and sinners came and ate with Jesus and his disciples.
verses.after: While Jesus was reclining at a meal in the house, many tax collectors and sinners came and reclined with him and his disciples.
verses.tsw_comparator: And as he reclined at table in the house, behold, many tax collectors and sinners came and were reclining with Jesus and his disciples.

verses.rationale: Keeps the question directed to disciples and the repeated social categories.

verses.after: The Pharisees saw this and asked his disciples, “Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And when the Pharisees saw this, they said to his disciples, “Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?”

verses.rationale: Preserves the compact analogy in ordinary spoken English.

verses.after: Jesus heard them and said, “Healthy people don’t need a doctor; sick people do.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when he heard it, he said, “Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick.

verses.rationale: Keeps the scriptural contrast and excludes an unprinted addition about repentance.

verses.after: Go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy, not sacrifice.’ For I came to call sinners, not the righteous.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy, and not sacrifice.’ For I came not to call the righteous, but sinners.”

verses.rationale: Preserves often and both groups without generalizing their practice.

verses.after: Then John’s disciples came to him. “Why do we and the Pharisees fast often,” they asked, “but your disciples don’t fast?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the disciples of John came to him, saying, “Why do we and the Pharisees fast often, but your disciples do not fast?”

verses.rationale: Renders sons of the bridal chamber accessibly and preserves the passive removal.

verses.after: Jesus said to them, “Can wedding guests mourn while the bridegroom is with them? The days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them. Then they will fast.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Jesus said to them, “Can the wedding guests mourn as long as the bridegroom is with them? The days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast.

verses.rationale: Makes the material action clear without allegorical explanation.
verses.before: No one puts a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment, because the patch pulls away from the garment and makes the tear worse.
verses.after: No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth onto an old garment. The patch pulls away from the garment, making the tear worse.
verses.tsw_comparator: No one puts a piece of unshrunk cloth on an old garment, for the patch tears away from the garment, and a worse tear is made.

verses.rationale: Preserves both kinds of loss and the final preservation of both.

verses.after: Nor do people put new wine into old wineskins. If they do, the skins burst, the wine spills, and the skins are ruined. They put new wine into fresh wineskins, and both are preserved.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Neither do people put new wine into old wineskins. If they do, the skins burst and the wine is spilled and the skins are destroyed. But new wine is put into fresh wineskins, and so both are preserved.”

verses.rationale: Retains has just died and avoids importing a different chronology or office.
verses.before: While Jesus was saying these things, a ruler came, bowed before him, and said, “My daughter has just died. But come, lay your hand on her, and she will live.”
verses.after: While he was telling them these things, a ruler came and bowed before him. “My daughter has just died,” he said. “But come and lay your hand on her, and she will live.”
verses.tsw_comparator: While he was saying these things to them, behold, a ruler came in and knelt before him, saying, “My daughter has just died, but come and lay your hand on her, and she will live.”

verses.rationale: Preserves Jesus now following the petitioner and the accompanying disciples.
verses.before: Jesus got up and followed him, along with his disciples.
verses.after: Jesus got up and followed him, along with his disciples.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Jesus rose and followed him, with his disciples.

verses.rationale: Retains duration, approach, and the particular part touched.
verses.before: And look—a woman who had been suffering from bleeding for twelve years came up behind him and touched the fringe of his cloak.
verses.after: Just then, a woman who had been bleeding for twelve years came up behind him and touched the fringe of his garment.
verses.tsw_comparator: And behold, a woman who had suffered from a discharge of blood for twelve years came up behind him and touched the fringe of his garment,

verses.rationale: Uses healed for contextual saved while retaining the conditional inner speech.
verses.before: For she was saying to herself, “If I only touch his cloak, I will be saved.”
verses.after: She had been saying to herself, “If I only touch his garment, I will be healed.”
verses.tsw_comparator: for she said to herself, “If I only touch his garment, I will be made well.”

verses.rationale: Keeps daughter and the repeated saving/healing language in its bodily setting.
verses.before: Jesus turned, saw her, and said, “Take courage, daughter. Your faith has saved you.” And the woman was made well from that hour.
verses.after: Jesus turned, saw her, and said, “Take courage, daughter. Your faith has made you well.” From that moment the woman was healed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jesus turned, and seeing her he said, “Take courage, daughter; your faith has made you well.” And the woman was made well from that hour.

verses.rationale: Retains the audible mourning scene without adding hired status.
verses.before: When Jesus came to the ruler's house and saw the flute players and the crowd making a commotion,
verses.after: When Jesus reached the ruler’s house, he saw the flute players and the noisy crowd.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when Jesus came to the ruler’s house and saw the flute players and the crowd making a commotion,

verses.rationale: Preserves Jesus’ assertion and ridicule without explaining sleep in the dialogue.
verses.before: he said, “Go away. The girl has not died but is sleeping.” And they laughed at him.
verses.after: “Go away,” he said. “The girl isn’t dead; she is sleeping.” But they laughed at him.
verses.tsw_comparator: he said, “Go away, for the girl is not dead but sleeping.” And they laughed at him.

verses.rationale: Keeps the passive removal and simple rising without added spectacle.
verses.before: After the crowd had been put outside, Jesus went in, took her by the hand, and the girl got up.
verses.after: After the crowd had been put outside, he went in and took her hand, and the girl got up.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when the crowd had been put outside, he went in and took her by the hand, and the girl arose.

verses.rationale: Keeps the local scope of the report.
verses.before: News about this spread throughout that entire region.
verses.after: News of this spread through that entire region.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the report of this went through all that district.

verses.rationale: Preserves two, the royal title, and the plea for mercy.
verses.before: As Jesus went on from there, two blind men followed him, crying out, “Have mercy on us, Son of David!”
verses.after: As Jesus went on from there, two blind men followed him, calling out, “Have mercy on us, Son of David!”
verses.tsw_comparator: And as Jesus passed on from there, two blind men followed him, crying aloud, “Have mercy on us, Son of David.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the question about ability and direct collective answer.
verses.before: When he entered the house, the blind men came to him. Jesus asked them, “Do you trust that I am able to do this?” They said to him, “Yes, Lord.”
verses.after: When he entered the house, the blind men came to him. Jesus asked them, “Do you believe I can do this?” “Yes, Lord,” they answered.
verses.tsw_comparator: When he entered the house, the blind men came to him, and Jesus said to them, “Do you believe that I am able to do this?” They said to him, “Yes, Lord.”

verses.rationale: Retains physical contact and according to without adding a measurable degree.
verses.before: Then he touched their eyes and said, “Let it happen for you according to your faith.”
verses.after: Then he touched their eyes and said, “Let it happen for you according to your faith.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he touched their eyes, saying, “According to your faith let it be done to you.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the strong warning rather than a casual request.
verses.before: Their eyes were opened. Jesus sternly warned them, “See that no one knows about this.”
verses.after: Their eyes were opened. Jesus warned them sternly, “See that no one learns about this.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And their eyes were opened. And Jesus sternly warned them, “See that no one knows about it.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the contrast between instruction and actual conduct.
verses.before: But they went out and spread news about him throughout that whole region.
verses.after: But they went out and spread news of him throughout that region.
verses.tsw_comparator: But they went away and spread his fame through all that district.

verses.rationale: Renders kophos by the speech outcome rather than assuming deafness.
verses.before: As they were going out, look—a demonized man who could not speak was brought to Jesus.
verses.after: As they were leaving, people brought him a demon-possessed man who could not speak.
verses.tsw_comparator: As they were going away, behold, a demon-oppressed man who was mute was brought to him.

verses.rationale: Preserves sequence and the crowd’s sweeping reported claim.
verses.before: After the demon was cast out, the man spoke. The crowds were amazed and said, “Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel.”
verses.after: Once the demon was driven out, the man spoke. The crowds were amazed and said, “Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel!”
verses.tsw_comparator: And when the demon had been cast out, the mute man spoke. And the crowds marveled, saying, “Never has anything like this been seen in Israel.”

verses.rationale: Retains the counterclaim without presenting it as narrator’s explanation.
verses.before: But the Pharisees said, “He casts out demons by the ruler of the demons.”
verses.after: But the Pharisees said, “He drives out demons by the ruler of demons.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But the Pharisees said, “He casts out demons by the ruler of demons.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the three coordinated activities and repeated every.
verses.before: Jesus went through all the towns and villages, teaching in their synagogues, proclaiming the good news of the kingdom, and healing every disease and every sickness.
verses.after: Jesus traveled through all the towns and villages, teaching in their synagogues, proclaiming the good news of the kingdom, and healing every disease and every infirmity.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Jesus went throughout all the cities and villages, teaching in their synagogues and proclaiming the good news of the kingdom and healing every disease and every affliction.

verses.rationale: Retains both conditions and the biblical shepherd image.
verses.before: When he saw the crowds, he had compassion on them because they were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd.
verses.after: When he saw the crowds, he was moved with compassion for them. They were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd.
verses.tsw_comparator: When he saw the crowds, he had compassion for them, because they were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd.

verses.rationale: Keeps the large harvest/small workforce contrast.
verses.before: Then he said to his disciples, “The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few.
verses.after: Then he told his disciples, “The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he said to his disciples, “The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few;

verses.rationale: Preserves ownership repeated in the appeal and destination.
verses.before: Therefore ask the Lord of the harvest to send out workers into his harvest.”
verses.after: So ask the Lord of the harvest to send workers out into his harvest.”
verses.tsw_comparator: therefore pray earnestly to the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into his harvest.”

verses.rationale: Keeps twelve and the authority linking this mission with Jesus’ work.
verses.before: Jesus called his twelve disciples and gave them authority over unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal every disease and every sickness.
verses.after: Jesus called his twelve disciples to him and gave them authority over unclean spirits, to drive them out and to heal every disease and every infirmity.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he called to him his twelve disciples and gave them authority over unclean spirits, to cast them out and to heal every disease and every affliction.

verses.rationale: Preserves first and the paired family relationships.
verses.before: These are the names of the twelve apostles: first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James son of Zebedee and John his brother;
verses.after: These are the names of the twelve apostles: first, Simon, called Peter, and his brother Andrew; James son of Zebedee and his brother John;
verses.tsw_comparator: The names of the twelve apostles are these: first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother;

verses.rationale: Retains all names and Matthew’s occupation without harmonizing alternate lists.
verses.before: Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James son of Alphaeus and Thaddaeus;
verses.after: Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James son of Alphaeus and Thaddaeus;
verses.tsw_comparator: Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus;

verses.rationale: Renders Kanana ios as a designation of zeal and links betrayal to handed over.
verses.before: Simon the Cananaean and Judas Iscariot, who also handed Jesus over.
verses.after: Simon the Zealot and Judas Iscariot, who also handed Jesus over.
verses.tsw_comparator: Simon the Zealot, and Judas Iscariot, who betrayed him.

verses.rationale: Preserves the restricted destination of this particular commission.
verses.before: Jesus sent out these twelve and instructed them: “Do not go onto a road of the Gentiles, and do not enter a Samaritan town.
verses.after: Jesus sent these twelve out with these instructions: “Do not go among the Gentiles or enter a Samaritan town.
verses.tsw_comparator: These twelve Jesus sent out, instructing them, “Go nowhere among the Gentiles and enter no town of the Samaritans,

verses.rationale: Keeps the house and sheep images without replacing them with an abstract audience.
verses.before: Go instead to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
verses.after: Go instead to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: but go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

verses.rationale: Matches the established proclamation formula and sense of nearness.
verses.before: As you go, proclaim, ‘The kingdom of heaven has drawn near.’
verses.after: As you go, proclaim, ‘The kingdom of heaven has come near.’
verses.tsw_comparator: And proclaim as you go, saying, ‘The kingdom of heaven has drawn near.’

verses.rationale: Preserves all four imperatives and the free receiving/giving balance.
verses.before: Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse those with skin diseases, and cast out demons. You received freely; give freely.
verses.after: Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse those with skin diseases, drive out demons. You received without paying; give without charging.
verses.tsw_comparator: Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse lepers, cast out demons. You received without payment; give without payment.

verses.rationale: Keeps all three metals and the ancient carrying image.
verses.before: Do not acquire gold, silver, or copper for your belts,
verses.after: Do not get gold, silver, or copper for your belts,
verses.tsw_comparator: Acquire no gold or silver or copper for your belts,

verses.rationale: Retains Matthew’s actual equipment restrictions without harmonizing other Gospels.
verses.before: no bag for the journey, no second tunic, sandals, or staff, because the worker deserves food.
verses.after: or a travel bag, or two tunics, or sandals, or a staff. A worker deserves food.
verses.tsw_comparator: no bag for your journey, or two tunics or sandals or a staff, for the laborer is worthy of his food.

verses.rationale: Preserves discernment of a host and stable lodging.
verses.before: Whatever town or village you enter, find out who there is worthy, and stay there until you leave.
verses.after: Whatever town or village you enter, find out who there is worthy, and stay with that person until you leave.
verses.tsw_comparator: And whatever town or village you enter, find out who is worthy in it and stay there until you depart.

verses.rationale: Keeps the household addressed through the house image.
verses.before: When you enter a house, greet it.
verses.after: As you enter the house, greet it.
verses.tsw_comparator: As you enter the house, greet it.

verses.rationale: Preserves the conditional movement of peace in both directions.
verses.before: If the house is worthy, let your peace come upon it. But if it is not worthy, let your peace return to you.
verses.after: If the house is worthy, let your peace rest on it. If it is not worthy, let your peace return to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if the house is worthy, let your peace come upon it, but if it is not worthy, let your peace return to you.

verses.rationale: Keeps both refusals and the embodied departure sign.
verses.before: If anyone will not welcome you or listen to your words, leave that house or town and shake the dust off your feet.
verses.after: If anyone will not welcome you or listen to your words, shake the dust from your feet as you leave that house or town.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if anyone will not receive you or listen to your words, shake off the dust from your feet when you leave that house or town.

verses.rationale: Preserves comparative judgment and both named cities.
verses.before: Truly I tell you, it will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that town.
verses.after: Truly I tell you, on the day of judgment it will be more bearable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah than for that town.
verses.tsw_comparator: Truly, I tell you, it will be more bearable on the day of judgment for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah than for that town.

verses.rationale: Retains all four animals and pairs practical discernment with innocence.
verses.before: “Look, I am sending you out like sheep among wolves. Therefore be wise as snakes and innocent as doves.
verses.after: “Look, I am sending you out like sheep among wolves. So be shrewd as snakes and innocent as doves.
verses.tsw_comparator: Behold, I am sending you out as sheep in the midst of wolves; so be wise as serpents and innocent as doves.

verses.rationale: Keeps concrete institutional persecution without generalizing it to all Jews.
verses.before: Be on guard against people, because they will hand you over to councils and flog you in their synagogues.
verses.after: Watch out for people. They will hand you over to councils and flog you in their synagogues.
verses.tsw_comparator: Beware of men, for they will hand you over to councils and flog you in their synagogues,

verses.rationale: Preserves purpose, audiences, and cause.
verses.before: You will be brought before governors and kings because of me, as a testimony to them and to the Gentiles.
verses.after: You will be brought before governors and kings because of me, as a testimony to them and to the Gentiles.
verses.tsw_comparator: and you will be brought before governors and kings for my sake, as a testimony to them and to the Gentiles.

verses.rationale: Keeps both anxieties and the passive gift at the needed moment.
verses.before: When they hand you over, do not be anxious about how or what you should speak, because what you are to say will be given to you in that hour.
verses.after: When they hand you over, do not worry about how to speak or what to say. What you should say will be given to you at that time.
verses.tsw_comparator: When they hand you over, do not be anxious how you are to speak or what you are to say, for what you are to say will be given to you in that hour.

verses.rationale: Preserves the personal Father relationship and Spirit’s agency.
verses.before: For it is not you speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you.
verses.after: For it will not be you speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you.
verses.tsw_comparator: For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the family roles and actual lethal consequences.
verses.before: Brother will hand over brother to death, and a father his child. Children will rise against parents and have them put to death.
verses.after: Brother will hand brother over to death, and a father his child. Children will turn against their parents and have them put to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: Brother will deliver brother over to death, and the father his child, and children will rise against parents and have them put to death,

verses.rationale: Retains the sweeping warning and future promise without resolving end’s referent.
verses.before: You will be hated by everyone because of my name. But the one who endures to the end will be saved.
verses.after: Everyone will hate you because of my name. But the one who endures to the end will be saved.
verses.tsw_comparator: and you will be hated by all for my name’s sake. But the one who endures to the end will be saved.

verses.rationale: Preserves the difficult temporal claim without inserting a later interpretive timetable.
verses.before: When they persecute you in one town, flee to the next. Truly I tell you, you will certainly not finish the towns of Israel before the Son of Man comes.
verses.after: When they persecute you in one town, flee to another. Truly I tell you, you will not finish the towns of Israel before the Son of Man comes.
verses.tsw_comparator: When they persecute you in one town, flee to the next, for truly, I tell you, you will not have gone through all the towns of Israel before the Son of Man comes.

verses.rationale: Keeps both unequal relationships and the source’s slave term.
verses.before: “A disciple is not above the teacher, nor a servant above the master.
verses.after: “A disciple is not above the teacher, nor a slave above the master.
verses.tsw_comparator: A disciple is not above his teacher, nor a servant above his master.

verses.rationale: Makes the elliptical final comparison readable while retaining the household image and name.
verses.before: It is enough for the disciple to become like the teacher and the servant like the master. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebul, how much more the members of his household!
verses.after: It is enough for the disciple to become like the teacher, and the slave like the master. If they have called the head of the house Beelzebul, how much more will they malign his household!
verses.tsw_comparator: It is enough for the disciple to be like his teacher, and the servant like his master. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebul, how much more those of his household.

verses.rationale: Preserves the paired disclosure assurances and their causal link.
verses.before: Therefore do not be afraid of them, because nothing is covered that will not be revealed, and nothing hidden that will not become known.
verses.after: So do not fear them. Nothing covered up will stay unrevealed, and nothing hidden will remain unknown.
verses.tsw_comparator: So have no fear of them, for nothing is covered that will not be revealed, or hidden that will not be known.

verses.rationale: Retains dark/light and ear/rooftop contrasts.
verses.before: What I tell you in the dark, say in the light; and what you hear whispered in your ear, proclaim from the housetops.
verses.after: What I tell you in the dark, speak in the light. What you hear whispered in your ear, proclaim from the rooftops.
verses.tsw_comparator: What I tell you in the dark, say in the light, and what you hear whispered, proclaim on the housetops.

verses.rationale: Keeps soul/body distinction and destroy without importing a theory of punishment.
verses.before: Do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the life. Fear instead the one who can destroy both life and body in Gehenna.
verses.after: Do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Fear instead the one who can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.
verses.tsw_comparator: And do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Rather fear him who can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.

verses.rationale: Retains coin and the source’s open apart-from phrase rather than specifying causation.
verses.before: Are not two sparrows sold for a small coin? Yet not one of them falls to the ground apart from your Father.
verses.after: Aren’t two sparrows sold for an assarion? Yet not one of them falls to the ground apart from your Father.
verses.tsw_comparator: Are not two sparrows sold for a penny? And not one of them will fall to the ground apart from your Father.

verses.rationale: Preserves the surprising totality of the image.
verses.before: Even the hairs of your head have all been counted.
verses.after: Even the hairs on your head have all been counted.
verses.tsw_comparator: But even the hairs of your head are all numbered.

verses.rationale: Keeps the many contrast and reassurance grounded in the preceding image.
verses.before: So do not be afraid. You are worth more than many sparrows.
verses.after: So do not be afraid. You are worth more than many sparrows.
verses.tsw_comparator: Fear not, therefore; you are of more value than many sparrows.

verses.rationale: Preserves reciprocal public acknowledgment.
verses.before: “Therefore everyone who acknowledges me before people, I also will acknowledge before my Father in heaven.
verses.after: “Everyone who acknowledges me before others, I too will acknowledge before my Father in heaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: So everyone who acknowledges me before men, I also will acknowledge before my Father who is in heaven,

verses.rationale: Keeps the exact opposing structure and consequence.
verses.before: But whoever denies me before people, I also will deny before my Father in heaven.
verses.after: But whoever denies me before others, I too will deny before my Father in heaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: but whoever denies me before men, I also will deny before my Father who is in heaven.

verses.rationale: Retains the sharp image before its explanation in family division.
verses.before: “Do not think that I came to bring peace to the earth. I did not come to bring peace, but a sword.
verses.after: “Do not think I came to bring peace to the earth. I came to bring a sword, not peace.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not think that I have come to bring peace to the earth. I have not come to bring peace, but a sword.

verses.rationale: Preserves all three specifically gendered relationships.
verses.before: For I came to set ‘a man against his father, a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law;
verses.after: For I came to set a man against his father, a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I have come to set a man against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law,

verses.rationale: Keeps the household focus of the preceding sword image.
verses.before: and a person's enemies will be members of their own household.’
verses.after: A person’s enemies will be members of that person’s own household.
verses.tsw_comparator: and a person’s enemies will be those of his own household.

verses.rationale: Preserves comparative love and both generations without substituting hatred.
verses.before: Whoever loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me, and whoever loves son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.
verses.after: Whoever loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me. Whoever loves son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me, and whoever loves son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.

verses.rationale: Retains the execution image and repeated worthiness language.
verses.before: Whoever does not take up their cross and follow after me is not worthy of me.
verses.after: Whoever does not take up their cross and follow me is not worthy of me.
verses.tsw_comparator: And whoever does not take his cross and follow me is not worthy of me.

verses.rationale: Keeps the paradox and explicit because-of-me qualification.
verses.before: Whoever finds their life will lose it, and whoever loses their life because of me will find it.
verses.after: Whoever finds their life will lose it, and whoever loses their life because of me will find it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever finds his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life for my sake will find it.

verses.rationale: Preserves the linked chain of welcome and sending.
verses.before: “Whoever welcomes you welcomes me, and whoever welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me.
verses.after: “Whoever welcomes you welcomes me, and whoever welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever receives you receives me, and whoever receives me receives him who sent me.

verses.rationale: Unfolds in the name of without losing the repeated identities and rewards.
verses.before: Whoever welcomes a prophet because they are a prophet will receive a prophet's reward, and whoever welcomes a righteous person because they are righteous will receive a righteous person's reward.
verses.after: Whoever welcomes a prophet because that person is a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward. Whoever welcomes a righteous person because that person is righteous will receive a righteous person’s reward.
verses.tsw_comparator: The one who receives a prophet because he is a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward, and the one who receives a righteous person because he is righteous will receive a righteous person’s reward.

verses.rationale: Preserves the small gift, little ones, disciple qualification, and emphatic assurance.
verses.before: And whoever gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones because they are a disciple—truly I tell you, that person will certainly not lose their reward.”
verses.after: And whoever gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones because that person is a disciple—truly I tell you, that giver will certainly not lose the reward.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And whoever gives one of these little ones even a cup of cold water because he is a disciple, truly, I tell you, he will by no means lose his reward.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the discourse conclusion and the source’s their without inventing a route.
verses.before: When Jesus finished instructing his twelve disciples, he left there to teach and proclaim in their towns.
verses.after: When Jesus finished instructing his twelve disciples, he left that place to teach and proclaim his message in their towns.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when Jesus had finished instructing his twelve disciples, he went on from there to teach and preach in their cities.

verses.rationale: Keeps imprisonment and Messiah as the narrator’s designation.
verses.before: When John heard in prison about the works of the Christ, he sent word through his disciples
verses.after: In prison, John heard about the Messiah’s deeds. He sent word through his disciples
verses.tsw_comparator: Now when John heard in prison about the works of the Christ, he sent word by his disciples

verses.rationale: Retains the coming-one expression and the genuine alternative in John’s question.
verses.before: and asked Jesus, “Are you the one who is coming, or should we expect someone else?”
verses.after: to ask Jesus, “Are you the one who is coming, or should we expect someone else?”
verses.tsw_comparator: and said to him, “Are you the one who is to come, or shall we look for another?”

verses.before: Jesus answered them, “Go and report to John what you hear and see:
verses.after: Jesus answered them, “Go and tell John what you hear and see:
verses.tsw_comparator: And Jesus answered them, “Go and tell John what you hear and see:

verses.rationale: Retains all six groups and distinguishes cleansing, healing, resurrection, and proclamation.
verses.before: blind people receive sight, those with impaired legs walk, people with skin diseases are cleansed, deaf people hear, the dead are raised, and the poor are told good news.
verses.after: the blind receive sight, the lame walk, people with skin diseases are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor hear good news.
verses.tsw_comparator: the blind receive their sight and the lame walk, lepers are cleansed and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have good news proclaimed to them.

verses.rationale: Preserves stumbling as an image rather than reducing it to intellectual disagreement.
verses.before: And blessed is anyone who does not stumble because of me.”
verses.after: And blessed is anyone who does not stumble because of me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And blessed is the one who is not offended by me.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated question and its unresolved image.
verses.before: As John's disciples were leaving, Jesus began speaking to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?
verses.after: As they were leaving, Jesus began speaking to the crowds about John. “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed swaying in the wind?

verses.rationale: Preserves the contrast between wilderness and luxury without elaborating motive.
verses.before: What then did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft clothing? Look, those who wear soft clothing are in kings' houses.

verses.tsw_comparator: What then did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.

verses.rationale: Keeps the quotation’s pronouns and double before-you emphasis.

verses.after: This is the one about whom it is written: ‘Look, I am sending my messenger ahead of you; he will prepare your way before you.’

verses.rationale: Preserves the birth idiom and startling comparison without assigning rank outside the text.

verses.after: Truly I tell you, among those born of women no one greater than John the Baptist has arisen. Yet the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he is.

verses.rationale: Chooses the passive reading of biazetai with the competing sense reserved for a note.

verses.after: And if you are willing to accept it, he is Elijah who is to come.

verses.rationale: Retains the brief listening refrain without an absent expansion.

verses.rationale: Keeps the rhetorical contrast without supplying an absolute dietary interpretation.

verses.after: John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, ‘He has a demon.’
verses.tsw_comparator: For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, ‘He has a demon.’

verses.rationale: Follows deeds rather than children and retains wisdom’s female personification.
verses.before: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, ‘Look, a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’ Yet wisdom is vindicated by her works.”
verses.after: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, ‘Look at him—a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’ Yet wisdom is vindicated by her deeds.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, ‘Look at him! A glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’ Yet wisdom is justified by her deeds.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the explicit reason for denunciation.
verses.before: Then Jesus began to denounce the towns where most of his works of power had been done, because they did not repent.
verses.after: Then he began denouncing the towns where most of his mighty works had taken place, because they had not repented.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he began to denounce the cities where most of his mighty works had been done, because they did not repent.

verses.rationale: Retains all four towns and the unreal comparison with visible repentance.
verses.before: “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! If the works of power done among you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.
verses.after: “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! If the mighty works done among you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.

verses.rationale: Keeps comparative rather than absolute judgment.
verses.before: But I tell you, it will be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgment than for you.
verses.after: But I tell you, on the day of judgment it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon than for you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I tell you, it will be more bearable on the day of judgment for Tyre and Sidon than for you.

verses.rationale: Retains the question, paired heights/depths, and unreal historical condition.

verses.after: And you, Capernaum—will you be lifted up to heaven? You will go down to Hades. If the mighty works done in you had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until today.
verses.tsw_comparator: And you, Capernaum, will you be exalted to heaven? You will be brought down to Hades. For if the mighty works done in you had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated warning and singular town addressee.
verses.before: But I tell you that it will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom on the day of judgment than for you.”
verses.after: But I tell you, on the day of judgment it will be more bearable for the land of Sodom than for you.”
