verses.rationale: Retains hidden/revealed contrast and the infant image without defining social classes.
verses.before: At that time Jesus said, “I praise you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and understanding and revealed them to little children.
verses.after: At that time Jesus said, “I praise you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and discerning and revealed them to little children.
verses.tsw_comparator: At that time Jesus answered and said, “I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you have hidden these things from the wise and understanding and revealed them to little children;

verses.rationale: Keeps the affirmation of the Father’s will in compact prayer speech.
verses.before: Yes, Father, because this was pleasing in your sight.
verses.after: Yes, Father, for this was your good pleasure.
verses.tsw_comparator: yes, Father, for such was your good pleasure.

verses.rationale: Preserves reciprocal knowledge and the final chosen recipient.
verses.before: Everything has been handed over to me by my Father. No one knows the Son except the Father, and no one knows the Father except the Son and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal him.
verses.after: “Everything has been handed over to me by my Father. No one knows the Son except the Father, and no one knows the Father except the Son and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal him.
verses.tsw_comparator: All things have been handed over to me by my Father, and no one knows the Son except the Father, and no one knows the Father except the Son and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal him.

verses.rationale: Retains both active toil and imposed load in a direct invitation.
verses.before: Come to me, all who are weary and carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest.
verses.after: Come to me, all of you who are weary from labor and weighed down, and I will give you rest.
verses.tsw_comparator: Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.

verses.rationale: Preserves yoke, learning, heart, and soul rather than flattening the images.
verses.before: Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, because I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your lives.
verses.after: Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, because I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.
verses.tsw_comparator: Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me, for I am gentle and lowly in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.

verses.rationale: Renders chrestos with its positive quality while retaining the paradox of restful burden.
verses.before: For my yoke is kind, and my burden is light.”
verses.after: For my yoke is kind, and my burden is light.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the need that prompts the disputed activity.
verses.before: At that time Jesus went through the grainfields on the Sabbath. His disciples were hungry and began picking heads of grain and eating them.
verses.after: At that time Jesus walked through grainfields on the Sabbath. His disciples were hungry and began picking heads of grain and eating them.
verses.tsw_comparator: At that time Jesus went through the grainfields on the Sabbath. His disciples were hungry, and they began to pluck heads of grain and to eat.

verses.rationale: Attributes the legal accusation to its speakers.
verses.before: When the Pharisees saw this, they said to him, “Look, your disciples are doing what is not lawful to do on the Sabbath.”
verses.after: The Pharisees saw it and told him, “Look! Your disciples are doing what is not permitted on the Sabbath.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But when the Pharisees saw it, they said to him, “Look, your disciples are doing what is not lawful to do on the Sabbath.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the appeal to reading and shared hunger.
verses.before: He said to them, “Have you not read what David did when he and those with him were hungry?
verses.after: He answered them, “Haven’t you read what David did when he and his companions were hungry?
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to them, “Have you not read what David did when he was hungry, and those who were with him:

verses.rationale: Follows plural ate and keeps the sacred bread’s recognizable designation.
verses.before: He entered the house of God and they ate the bread of the Presence, which was not lawful for him or those with him to eat, but only for the priests.
verses.after: He entered the house of God, and they ate the bread of the Presence, which neither he nor his companions were permitted to eat—only the priests.
verses.tsw_comparator: how he entered the house of God and ate the bread of the Presence, which it was not lawful for him to eat, nor for those who were with him, but only for the priests?

verses.rationale: Retains the provocative profane/innocent contrast.
verses.before: Or have you not read in the Law that on the Sabbath the priests in the temple break the Sabbath and are innocent?
verses.after: Or haven’t you read in the Law that on Sabbaths the priests in the temple profane the Sabbath and yet are innocent?
verses.tsw_comparator: Or have you not read in the Law how on the Sabbath the priests in the temple profane the Sabbath and are guiltless?

verses.rationale: Preserves the neuter something without imposing a personal paraphrase.
verses.before: But I tell you, something greater than the temple is here.
verses.after: I tell you, something greater than the temple is here.
verses.tsw_comparator: I tell you, something greater than the temple is here.

verses.rationale: Repeats the earlier quotation identically and preserves its practical consequence.
verses.before: If you had known what this means, ‘I desire mercy and not sacrifice,’ you would not have condemned the innocent.
verses.after: If you had understood, ‘I desire mercy, not sacrifice,’ you would not have condemned the innocent.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if you had known what this means, ‘I desire mercy, and not sacrifice,’ you would not have condemned the guiltless.

verses.rationale: Keeps the title and explicit relation of authority.
verses.before: For the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
verses.after: For the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For the Son of Man is lord of the Sabbath.”

verses.rationale: Preserves their without broad ethnic editorializing.
verses.before: Jesus left there and entered their synagogue.
verses.after: He left that place and entered their synagogue.
verses.tsw_comparator: He went on from there and entered their synagogue.

verses.rationale: Separates the question from the narrator’s stated hostile purpose.
verses.before: And look—a man there had a withered hand. They asked Jesus, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?” so that they might accuse him.
verses.after: A man with a withered hand was there. They asked Jesus, “Is it permitted to heal on the Sabbath?” They wanted grounds to accuse him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And behold, there was a man with a withered hand. And they asked him, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?”—so that they might accuse him.

verses.rationale: Retains the single animal and concrete rescue actions.
verses.before: He said to them, “Which one of you, if you have a sheep that falls into a pit on the Sabbath, will not take hold of it and lift it out?
verses.after: He said to them, “If one of you has a sheep and it falls into a pit on the Sabbath, won’t you take hold of it and lift it out?
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to them, “Which one of you who has a sheep, if it falls into a pit on the Sabbath, will not take hold of it and lift it out?

verses.rationale: Keeps the comparative argument and broad do-good conclusion.
verses.before: How much more valuable is a human being than a sheep! Therefore it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath.”
verses.after: How much more valuable a human being is than a sheep! So it is permitted to do good on the Sabbath.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Of how much more value is a man than a sheep! So it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath.”

verses.rationale: Preserves command, response, and bodily comparison.
verses.before: Then he said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out, and it was restored, healthy like the other.
verses.after: Then he told the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out, and it was restored, as healthy as the other.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” And he stretched it out, and it was restored, whole like the other.

verses.rationale: Keeps the real threat rather than softening it to disagreement.
verses.before: But the Pharisees went out and plotted against Jesus, how they might destroy him.
verses.after: The Pharisees went out and plotted against him, discussing how to destroy him.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the Pharisees went out and conspired against him, how to destroy him.

verses.rationale: Preserves withdrawal and all without adding crowds to the pinned phrase.
verses.before: Knowing this, Jesus withdrew from there. Many followed him, and he healed them all.
verses.after: Jesus learned of this and withdrew. Many followed him, and he healed them all.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jesus, aware of this, withdrew from there. And many followed him, and he healed them all

verses.rationale: Keeps the strong prohibition and its personal object.
verses.before: He warned them not to make him known,
verses.after: He warned them not to make him known.
verses.tsw_comparator: and ordered them not to make him known.

verses.rationale: Leaves the fulfillment introduction connected to the following quotation.
verses.before: so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled:
verses.after: This fulfilled what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah:
verses.tsw_comparator: This was to fulfill what was spoken by the prophet Isaiah:

verses.rationale: Retains servant, soul, Spirit, and justice with the nations as recipients.
verses.before: “Look, my servant whom I chose, my beloved, in whom my soul delights. I will put my Spirit upon him, and he will announce justice to the Gentiles.
verses.after: “Here is my servant, whom I have chosen, my beloved, in whom my soul delights. I will put my Spirit upon him, and he will announce justice to the nations.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Behold my servant whom I have chosen, my beloved with whom my soul is well pleased. I will put my Spirit upon him, and he will proclaim justice to the Gentiles.

verses.rationale: Keeps the paired negatives and public setting of the quotation.
verses.before: He will not quarrel or cry out, and no one will hear his voice in the streets.
verses.after: He will not quarrel or shout; no one will hear his voice in the streets.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will not quarrel or cry aloud, nor will anyone hear his voice in the streets;

verses.rationale: Preserves fragile objects and the unusual justice-to-victory movement.
verses.before: A crushed reed he will not break, and a smoldering wick he will not extinguish, until he brings justice to victory.
verses.after: He will not break a crushed reed or put out a smoldering wick, until he brings justice through to victory.
verses.tsw_comparator: a bruised reed he will not break, and a smoldering wick he will not quench, until he brings justice to victory;

verses.rationale: Retains name and nations rather than substituting abstract universalism.
verses.before: And in his name the Gentiles will hope.”
verses.after: And the nations will hope in his name.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and in his name the Gentiles will hope.”

verses.rationale: Keeps both disabilities and both outcomes in source order.
verses.before: Then a demonized man who was blind and unable to speak was brought to him. Jesus healed him, so that the man spoke and saw.
verses.after: Then a demon-possessed man who was blind and unable to speak was brought to him. Jesus healed him, so that the man could speak and see.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then a demon-oppressed man who was blind and mute was brought to him, and he healed him, so that the man spoke and saw.

verses.rationale: Preserves the tentative question rather than turning it into a confession.
verses.before: All the crowds were amazed and said, “Could this be the Son of David?”
verses.after: All the crowds were astonished. “Could this be the Son of David?” they asked.
verses.tsw_comparator: And all the people were amazed, and said, “Can this be the Son of David?”

verses.rationale: Keeps the exclusive accusation and named ruler.
verses.before: But when the Pharisees heard, they said, “This man does not cast out demons except by Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons.”
verses.after: But when the Pharisees heard this, they said, “This man drives out demons only by Beelzebul, the ruler of demons.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But when the Pharisees heard it, they said, “It is only by Beelzebul, the ruler of demons, that this man casts out demons.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the three scales of division and resulting ruin.
verses.before: Knowing their thoughts, Jesus said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to ruin, and no city or house divided against itself will stand.
verses.after: Knowing their thoughts, he said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste. No town or household divided against itself will stand.
verses.tsw_comparator: Knowing their thoughts, he said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and no city or house divided against itself will stand.

verses.rationale: Keeps the reductive hypothetical and repeated name.
verses.before: If Satan casts out Satan, he is divided against himself. How then will his kingdom stand?
verses.after: If Satan drives out Satan, he is divided against himself. How then will his kingdom stand?
verses.tsw_comparator: And if Satan casts out Satan, he is divided against himself. How then will his kingdom stand?

verses.rationale: Renders your sons contextually while preserving the challenge from their own group.
verses.before: And if I cast out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges.
verses.after: And if I drive out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your own followers drive them out? So they will be your judges.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if I cast out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges.

verses.rationale: Retains the Spirit and actual arrival rather than merely future nearness.
verses.before: But if I cast out demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
verses.after: But if I drive out demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has reached you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if it is by the Spirit of God that I cast out demons, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the violent house image and required sequence.
verses.before: Or how can someone enter a strong man's house and plunder his possessions unless he first binds the strong man? Then he will plunder his house.
verses.after: How can anyone enter a strong man’s house and seize his belongings without first tying up the strong man? Only then can the house be plundered.
verses.tsw_comparator: Or how can someone enter a strong man’s house and plunder his goods, unless he first binds the strong man? Then indeed he may plunder his house.

verses.rationale: Preserves the two unqualified antitheses in this context.
verses.before: Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.
verses.after: Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.

verses.rationale: Keeps the breadth of forgiveness and precise exception.
verses.before: “Therefore I tell you, every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven people, but blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven.
verses.after: That is why I tell you: every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven people, but blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I tell you, every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven people, but the blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven.

verses.rationale: Preserves the distinct objects and two-age formulation without an added doctrinal system.
verses.before: Whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, either in this age or in the age to come.
verses.after: Anyone who speaks against the Son of Man will be forgiven. But anyone who speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, either in this age or in the age to come.
verses.tsw_comparator: And whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, either in this age or in the age to come.

verses.rationale: Keeps the imperative form and consistent tree/fruit character.
verses.before: “Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree bad and its fruit bad, because a tree is known by its fruit.
verses.after: “Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree rotten and its fruit rotten. A tree is recognized by its fruit.
verses.tsw_comparator: Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree bad and its fruit bad, for the tree is known by its fruit.

verses.rationale: Retains the insult and bodily abundance image.
verses.before: Brood of vipers! How can you speak good things when you are evil? For the mouth speaks from the abundance of the heart.
verses.after: You brood of vipers! How can you speak good things when you are evil? The mouth speaks from what overflows from the heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: You brood of vipers! How can you speak good, when you are evil? For out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated good/evil without importing heart into an unprinted phrase.
verses.before: A good person brings good things out of a good treasury, and an evil person brings evil things out of an evil treasury.
verses.after: A good person brings good things out of a good store, and an evil person brings evil things out of an evil store.
verses.tsw_comparator: The good person out of his good treasure brings forth good, and the evil person out of his evil treasure brings forth evil.

verses.rationale: Keeps every and the accounting image.
verses.before: I tell you that on the day of judgment people will give account for every careless word they speak.
verses.after: I tell you, people will give an account on the day of judgment for every careless word they speak.
verses.tsw_comparator: I tell you, on the day of judgment people will give account for every careless word they speak,

verses.rationale: Preserves the judicial alternatives and repeated basis.
verses.before: For by your words you will be set right, and by your words you will be condemned.”
verses.after: For by your words you will be vindicated, and by your words you will be condemned.”
verses.tsw_comparator: for by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.”

verses.rationale: Keeps some and the request’s source qualification.
verses.before: Then some of the scribes and Pharisees answered him, “Teacher, we want to see a sign from you.”
verses.after: Then some scribes and Pharisees said to him, “Teacher, we want to see a sign from you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then some of the scribes and Pharisees answered him, saying, “Teacher, we wish to see a sign from you.”

verses.rationale: Retains adulterous as covenantal imagery without substituting an explanation.
verses.before: He answered them, “An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, but no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah the prophet.
verses.after: He answered, “An evil and adulterous generation demands a sign, but no sign will be given to it except the sign of the prophet Jonah.
verses.tsw_comparator: But he answered them, “An evil and adulterous generation seeks for a sign, but no sign will be given to it except the sign of the prophet Jonah.

verses.rationale: Keeps exact durations and both bodily location images without chronological harmonization.
verses.before: For just as Jonah was in the belly of the great fish three days and three nights, so the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth three days and three nights.
verses.after: Just as Jonah was in the belly of the sea creature for three days and three nights, so the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth for three days and three nights.
verses.tsw_comparator: For just as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the great fish, so will the Son of Man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.

verses.rationale: Preserves male reference, repentance, and neuter something greater.
verses.before: The people of Nineveh will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at Jonah's proclamation—and look, something greater than Jonah is here.
verses.after: The men of Nineveh will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at Jonah’s proclamation. And look—something greater than Jonah is here.
verses.tsw_comparator: The men of Nineveh will rise up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and behold, something greater than Jonah is here.

verses.rationale: Keeps her title, journey, and the repeated comparison.
verses.before: The queen of the south will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon's wisdom—and look, something greater than Solomon is here.
verses.after: The queen of the South will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon’s wisdom. And look—something greater than Solomon is here.
verses.tsw_comparator: The queen of the South will rise up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and behold, something greater than Solomon is here.

verses.rationale: Retains the spirit’s movement and failed search without modern diagnosis.
verses.before: “When an unclean spirit comes out of a person, it passes through waterless places looking for rest and does not find it.
verses.after: “When an unclean spirit leaves a person, it travels through waterless places seeking rest, but finds none.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the unclean spirit has gone out of a person, it passes through waterless places seeking rest, but finds none.

verses.rationale: Keeps the three conditions that set up the return.
verses.before: Then it says, ‘I will return to my house that I left.’ When it comes, it finds the house empty, swept, and put in order.
verses.after: Then it says, ‘I will return to the house I left.’ When it arrives, it finds the house empty, swept, and put in order.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then it says, ‘I will return to my house from which I came.’ And when it comes, it finds the house empty, swept, and put in order.

verses.rationale: Preserves seven, escalation, and the explicit application to the generation.
verses.before: Then it goes and brings with it seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they enter and live there. The final condition of that person becomes worse than the first. So it will also be with this evil generation.”
verses.after: Then it goes and brings seven other spirits more evil than itself. They enter and settle there, and that person’s final condition becomes worse than the first. So it will be with this evil generation.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then it goes and brings with it seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they enter and dwell there, and the last state of that person is worse than the first. So also will it be with this evil generation.”

verses.rationale: Retains the familial terms without resolving later kinship debates.
verses.before: While Jesus was still speaking to the crowds, look—his mother and brothers stood outside, wanting to speak with him.
verses.after: While he was still speaking to the crowds, his mother and brothers were standing outside, wanting to speak to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: While he was still speaking to the crowds, behold, his mother and his brothers stood outside, asking to speak to him.

verses.rationale: Retains the entire verse printed in the pinned edition.
verses.before: Someone told him, “Look, your mother and your brothers are standing outside, wanting to speak with you.”
verses.after: Someone told him, “Your mother and brothers are standing outside, wanting to speak to you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Someone told him, “Your mother and your brothers are standing outside, asking to speak to you.”

verses.rationale: Makes the immediate addressee clear and preserves both questions.
verses.before: But Jesus answered the person who told him, “Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?”
verses.after: He answered the person who told him, “Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?”
verses.tsw_comparator: But he replied to the man who told him, “Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?”

verses.rationale: Retains the identifying gesture and family language.
verses.before: Stretching out his hand toward his disciples, he said, “Look—my mother and my brothers!
verses.after: Stretching his hand toward his disciples, he said, “Here are my mother and my brothers!
verses.tsw_comparator: And stretching out his hand toward his disciples, he said, “Here are my mother and my brothers!

verses.rationale: Keeps all three kinship roles, including the newly explicit sister.
verses.before: Whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother and sister and mother.”
verses.after: For whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother and sister and mother.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother and sister and mother.”

verses.rationale: Preserves temporal continuity and the teaching posture.
verses.before: That same day Jesus went out of the house and sat beside the sea.
verses.after: That same day Jesus left the house and sat beside the sea.
verses.tsw_comparator: That same day Jesus went out of the house and sat beside the sea.

verses.rationale: Keeps seated teacher/standing crowd and their different locations.
verses.before: Such large crowds gathered around him that he got into a boat and sat down, while the whole crowd stood on the shore.
verses.after: Large crowds gathered around him, so he got into a boat and sat there while the whole crowd stood on the shore.
verses.tsw_comparator: And great crowds gathered about him, so that he got into a boat and sat down. And the whole crowd stood on the shore.

verses.rationale: Retains parable and the sower/sow repetition.
verses.before: He told them many things in parables: “Look, a sower went out to sow.
verses.after: He told them many things in parables: “Listen! A sower went out to sow.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he told them many things in parables, saying: “Behold, a sower went out to sow.

verses.rationale: Makes plural seeds explicit from the grammatical object.
verses.before: As he sowed, some seed fell along the path, and the birds came and ate it.
verses.after: As he sowed, some seeds fell beside the path, and birds came and ate them.
verses.tsw_comparator: And as he sowed, some seeds fell along the path, and the birds came and devoured them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the stated cause rather than correcting the agricultural image.
verses.before: Other seed fell on rocky ground where it did not have much soil. It sprang up quickly because the soil was shallow.
verses.after: Others fell on rocky ground with little soil. They sprouted at once because the soil was shallow.
verses.tsw_comparator: Other seeds fell on rocky ground, where they did not have much soil, and immediately they sprang up, since they had no depth of soil,

verses.rationale: Keeps both causal stages and the singular collective root.
verses.before: But when the sun rose, it was scorched, and because it had no root, it withered.
verses.after: But when the sun rose, they were scorched. Because they had no root, they withered.
verses.tsw_comparator: but when the sun rose they were scorched; and since they had no root, they withered away.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated thorns and the choking image.
verses.before: Other seed fell among thorns, and the thorns grew up and choked it.
verses.after: Others fell among thorns. The thorns grew up and choked them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Other seeds fell among thorns, and the thorns grew up and choked them.

verses.rationale: Preserves all yields in Matthew’s descending order.
verses.before: Other seed fell on good soil and produced fruit—some a hundredfold, some sixty, and some thirty.
verses.after: Others fell on good soil and produced a crop: some a hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.
verses.tsw_comparator: Other seeds fell on good soil and produced grain, some a hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.

verses.rationale: Matches the established concise refrain.
verses.before: Let anyone with ears listen.”
verses.after: Let anyone with ears listen.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He who has ears, let him hear.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the distinction between disciples and them.
verses.before: The disciples came and asked him, “Why do you speak to them in parables?”
verses.after: The disciples came to him and asked, “Why do you speak to them in parables?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the disciples came and said to him, “Why do you speak to them in parables?”

verses.rationale: Keeps given knowledge and mysteries rather than making them merely puzzles.
verses.before: He answered, “To you it has been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it has not been given.
verses.after: He answered, “You have been given knowledge of the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but they have not.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he answered them, “To you it has been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it has not been given.

verses.rationale: Preserves the paradox without supplying an unstated object of possession.
verses.before: For whoever has, more will be given, and they will have abundance. But whoever does not have, even what they have will be taken away.
verses.after: For whoever has will be given more and will have abundance. But whoever does not have will lose even what they have.
verses.tsw_comparator: For to the one who has, more will be given, and he will have abundance, but from the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away.

verses.rationale: Retains Matthew’s because relation and repeated perception terms.
verses.before: This is why I speak to them in parables: because though seeing, they do not see; and though hearing, they do not hear or understand.
verses.after: That is why I speak to them in parables: though they see, they do not see; though they hear, they do not hear or understand.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is why I speak to them in parables, because seeing they do not see, and hearing they do not hear, nor do they understand.

verses.rationale: Keeps emphatic repeated action and emphatic denial as poetry.
verses.before: In them Isaiah's prophecy is fulfilled: ‘You will indeed hear but never understand, and you will indeed see but never perceive.
verses.after: In them Isaiah’s prophecy is fulfilled: ‘You will hear and hear, but never understand; you will look and look, but never see.
verses.tsw_comparator: Indeed, in their case the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled that says: ‘You will indeed hear but never understand, and you will indeed see but never perceive.

verses.rationale: Preserves human eye-closing and every member of the extended sensory pattern.
verses.before: For this people's heart has become dull; they hear with heavy ears, and they have closed their eyes, so that they might not see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their heart, turn, and I would heal them.’
verses.after: For this people’s heart has grown dull. Their ears are hard of hearing, and they have closed their eyes, so that they might not see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their heart, and turn—and I would heal them.’
verses.tsw_comparator: For this people’s heart has grown dull, and with their ears they can barely hear, and their eyes they have closed, lest they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart and turn, and I would heal them.’

verses.rationale: Retains blessing addressed to the disciples’ organs of perception.
verses.before: But blessed are your eyes because they see, and your ears because they hear.
verses.after: But blessed are your eyes, because they see, and your ears, because they hear.
verses.tsw_comparator: But blessed are your eyes, for they see, and your ears, for they hear.

verses.rationale: Keeps all repeated verbs and the contrast across generations.
verses.before: Truly I tell you, many prophets and righteous people longed to see what you see and did not see it, and to hear what you hear and did not hear it.
verses.after: Truly I tell you, many prophets and righteous people longed to see what you see but did not see it, and to hear what you hear but did not hear it.
verses.tsw_comparator: For truly, I say to you, many prophets and righteous people longed to see what you see, and did not see it, and to hear what you hear, and did not hear it.

verses.rationale: Preserves the invitation introducing the interpretation.
verses.before: “So hear the parable of the sower.
verses.after: “So listen to the parable of the sower.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Hear then the parable of the sower:

verses.rationale: Keeps the shifting seed/person metaphor rather than smoothing it away.
verses.before: When anyone hears the word of the kingdom and does not understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away what was sown in the heart. This is what was sown along the path.
verses.after: When anyone hears the word of the kingdom without understanding it, the evil one comes and snatches away what was sown in that person’s heart. This is the one sown beside the path.
verses.tsw_comparator: When anyone hears the word of the kingdom and does not understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away what has been sown in his heart. This is what was sown along the path.

verses.rationale: Preserves immediate joy and the unfinished contrast across labels.
verses.before: What was sown on rocky ground is the one who hears the word and immediately receives it with joy,
verses.after: The one sown on rocky ground is someone who hears the word and immediately receives it with joy,
verses.tsw_comparator: As for what was sown on rocky ground, this is the one who hears the word and immediately receives it with joy,

verses.rationale: Keeps both pressures, their cause, and the repeated immediacy.
verses.before: yet has no root within and lasts only a while. When trouble or persecution comes because of the word, that person immediately falls away.
verses.after: but has no root within and lasts only a little while. When trouble or persecution comes because of the word, that person immediately falls away.
verses.tsw_comparator: yet he has no root in himself, but endures for a while, and when tribulation or persecution arises on account of the word, immediately he falls away.

verses.rationale: Preserves wealth’s deception and the word as the choked object.
verses.before: What was sown among thorns is the one who hears the word, but the anxiety of the age and the deception of wealth choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
verses.after: The one sown among thorns hears the word, but the anxiety of this age and the deceitfulness of wealth choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for what was sown among thorns, this is the one who hears the word, but the cares of the age and the deceitfulness of riches choke the word, and it proves unfruitful.

verses.rationale: Keeps understanding linked to fruit and repeats the descending yields.
verses.before: But what was sown on good soil is the one who hears the word and understands it, who indeed bears fruit and produces—one a hundredfold, another sixty, another thirty.”
verses.after: The one sown on good soil hears the word and understands it. That person bears fruit and produces a hundredfold, or sixty, or thirty.”
verses.tsw_comparator: As for what was sown on good soil, this is the one who hears the word and understands it. He indeed bears fruit and yields, in one case a hundredfold, in another sixty, and in another thirty.”

verses.rationale: Retains kingdom comparison and ownership of the field.
verses.before: He put another parable before them: “The kingdom of heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field.
verses.after: He set another parable before them: “The kingdom of heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field.
verses.tsw_comparator: He put another parable before them, saying, “The kingdom of heaven may be compared to a man who sowed good seed in his field,

verses.rationale: Keeps the specific weed term for vocabulary explanation and the covert sequence.
verses.before: But while everyone was sleeping, his enemy came, sowed weeds among the wheat, and went away.
verses.after: While people were sleeping, his enemy came, sowed darnel among the wheat, and went away.
verses.tsw_comparator: but while his men were sleeping, his enemy came and sowed weeds among the wheat and went away.

verses.rationale: Preserves the stage at which the intrusion becomes visible.
verses.before: When the plants grew and produced grain, then the weeds also appeared.
verses.after: When the plants sprouted and formed grain, the darnel appeared as well.
verses.tsw_comparator: So when the plants came up and bore grain, then the weeds appeared also.

verses.rationale: Retains slavery and their puzzled double question.
verses.before: The landowner's servants came and said to him, ‘Master, did you not sow good seed in your field? Where did the weeds come from?’
verses.after: The owner’s slaves came and asked him, ‘Master, didn’t you sow good seed in your field? Where did the darnel come from?’
verses.tsw_comparator: And the servants of the master of the house came and said to him, ‘Master, did you not sow good seed in your field? How then does it have weeds?’

verses.rationale: Keeps the identified agent and the proposed intervention.
verses.before: He told them, ‘An enemy did this.’ The servants asked, ‘Do you want us to go and gather them?’
verses.after: ‘An enemy has done this,’ he told them. The slaves asked him, ‘Do you want us to go and gather it?’
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to them, ‘An enemy has done this.’ So the servants said to him, ‘Then do you want us to go and gather them?’

verses.rationale: Preserves the reason for delay as protection of wheat.
verses.before: But he said, ‘No, because when you gather the weeds you might uproot the wheat with them.
verses.after: ‘No,’ he said. ‘While gathering the darnel you might uproot the wheat along with it.
verses.tsw_comparator: But he said, ‘No, lest in gathering the weeds you root up the wheat along with them.

verses.rationale: Keeps both outcomes and their specified order.
verses.before: Let both grow together until the harvest. At harvest time I will tell the harvesters: Gather the weeds first and tie them into bundles to burn them, but gather the wheat into my barn.’”
verses.after: Let both grow together until the harvest. At harvest time I will tell the reapers: Gather the darnel first and tie it in bundles to burn, but bring the wheat into my barn.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Let both grow together until the harvest, and at harvest time I will tell the reapers, “Gather the weeds first and bind them in bundles to be burned, but gather the wheat into my barn.”’”

verses.rationale: Preserves the parallel opening and the concrete small seed.
verses.before: He put another parable before them: “The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that a man took and sowed in his field.
verses.after: He set another parable before them: “The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that a man took and sowed in his field.
verses.tsw_comparator: He put another parable before them, saying, “The kingdom of heaven is like a grain of mustard seed that a man took and sowed in his field.

verses.rationale: Retains the source’s broad size claim and tree image without botanical correction.
verses.before: It is smaller than all the other seeds, but when it grows it becomes larger than the garden plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the sky come and nest in its branches.”
verses.after: It is smaller than all the seeds, but when it grows it is larger than the garden plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the sky come and nest in its branches.”
verses.tsw_comparator: It is the smallest of all seeds, but when it has grown it is larger than all the garden plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and make nests in its branches.”

verses.rationale: Preserves female agency, hidden leaven, exact measures, and complete effect.
verses.before: He told them another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like yeast that a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour until all of it was leavened.”
verses.after: He told them another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like leaven that a woman took and hid in three measures of flour until it was all leavened.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He told them another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like leaven that a woman took and hid in three measures of flour, till it was all leavened.”

verses.rationale: Retains the narrative’s broad statement in its discourse setting.
verses.before: Jesus spoke all these things to the crowds in parables, and he did not speak to them without a parable,
verses.after: Jesus spoke all these things to the crowds in parables. He said nothing to them without a parable,
verses.tsw_comparator: All these things Jesus said to the crowds in parables; indeed, he said nothing to them without a parable.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned text without adding world or a prophet’s name.
verses.before: so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled: “I will open my mouth in parables; I will proclaim things hidden from the foundation of the world.”
verses.after: fulfilling what was spoken through the prophet: “I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden since the foundation.”
verses.tsw_comparator: This was to fulfill what was spoken by the prophet: “I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter what has been hidden since the foundation of the world.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the move to private interpretation and the disciples’ stated request.
verses.before: Then Jesus left the crowds and went into the house. His disciples came to him and said, “Explain to us the parable of the weeds in the field.”
verses.after: Then he left the crowds and went into the house. His disciples came to him and said, “Explain the parable of the darnel in the field to us.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he left the crowds and went into the house. And his disciples came to him, saying, “Explain to us the parable of the weeds of the field.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the first explicit identification in the explanation.
verses.before: He answered, “The one sowing the good seed is the Son of Man.
verses.after: He answered, “The one who sows the good seed is the Son of Man.
verses.tsw_comparator: He answered, “The one who sows the good seed is the Son of Man.

verses.rationale: Retains world rather than church and the parallel family identities.
verses.before: The field is the world. The good seed are the children of the kingdom; the weeds are the children of the evil one.
verses.after: The field is the world. The good seed are the children of the kingdom; the darnel are the children of the evil one.
verses.tsw_comparator: The field is the world, and the good seed is the sons of the kingdom. The weeds are the sons of the evil one,

verses.rationale: Distinguishes world from age and preserves every interpretation.
verses.before: The enemy who sowed them is the devil. The harvest is the completion of the age, and the harvesters are angels.
verses.after: The enemy who sowed them is the devil. The harvest is the completion of the age, and the reapers are angels.
verses.tsw_comparator: and the enemy who sowed them is the devil. The harvest is the end of the age, and the reapers are angels.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated age ending and the actual burning image.
verses.before: Therefore, just as the weeds are gathered and burned with fire, so it will be at the completion of the age.
verses.after: Just as darnel is gathered and burned in fire, so it will be at the completion of the age.
verses.tsw_comparator: Just as the weeds are gathered and burned with fire, so will it be at the end of the age.

verses.rationale: Preserves causes and persons as distinguishable objects of removal.
verses.before: The Son of Man will send his angels, and they will gather out of his kingdom everything that causes stumbling and everyone who practices lawlessness.
verses.after: The Son of Man will send his angels, and they will gather out of his kingdom everything that causes stumbling and everyone who practices lawlessness.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Son of Man will send his angels, and they will gather out of his kingdom all causes of sin and all law-breakers,

verses.rationale: Keeps the furnace and established judgment refrain.
verses.before: They will throw them into the furnace of fire. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth.
verses.after: They will throw them into the blazing furnace. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth.
verses.tsw_comparator: and throw them into the fiery furnace. In that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

verses.rationale: Retains brightness, Father relationship, and listening refrain.
verses.before: Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Let anyone with ears listen.
verses.after: Then the righteous will shine like the sun in their Father’s kingdom. Let anyone with ears listen.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. He who has ears, let him hear.

verses.rationale: Keeps joy as motive and does not supply an ethical verdict absent from the parable.
verses.before: “The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field. A man found it and hid it again, and in his joy he goes and sells everything he has and buys that field.
verses.after: “The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field. A man found it and hid it again. In his joy he goes and sells everything he has and buys that field.
verses.tsw_comparator: “The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field, which a man found and covered up. Then in his joy he goes and sells all that he has and buys that field.

verses.rationale: Preserves the kingdom’s comparison to the searching merchant.
verses.before: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant searching for fine pearls.
verses.after: “Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant searching for fine pearls.
verses.tsw_comparator: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant in search of fine pearls,

verses.rationale: Keeps the one pearl and total sale distinct from the prior field story.
verses.before: When he found one pearl of great value, he went, sold everything he had, and bought it.
verses.after: When he found one pearl of great value, he went and sold everything he had and bought it.
verses.tsw_comparator: who, on finding one pearl of great value, went and sold all that he had and bought it.

verses.rationale: Retains the net type and comprehensive mixture.
verses.before: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a net thrown into the sea that gathered fish of every kind.
verses.after: “Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a dragnet thrown into the sea that gathered fish of every kind.
verses.tsw_comparator: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a net that was thrown into the sea and gathered fish of every kind.

verses.rationale: Preserves fullness, sorting posture, and opposed destinations.
verses.before: When it was full, they pulled it onto the shore, sat down, gathered the good fish into containers, and threw the bad away.
verses.after: When it was full, they pulled it ashore, sat down, and sorted the good fish into containers, throwing the worthless ones away.
verses.tsw_comparator: When it was full, men drew it ashore and sat down and sorted the good into containers but threw away the bad.

verses.rationale: Keeps the interpretation’s agents and direction of separation.
verses.before: So it will be at the completion of the age. The angels will go out, separate the evil from among the righteous,
verses.after: So it will be at the completion of the age. The angels will come out and separate the evil from among the righteous
verses.tsw_comparator: So it will be at the end of the age. The angels will come out and separate the evil from the righteous

verses.rationale: Repeats the exact judgment refrain from the earlier explanation.
verses.before: and throw them into the furnace of fire. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth.”
verses.after: and throw them into the blazing furnace. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth.
verses.tsw_comparator: and throw them into the fiery furnace. In that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned short answer without adding Lord.
verses.before: “Have you understood all these things?” They said to him, “Yes.”
verses.after: “Have you understood all these things?” They answered him, “Yes.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Have you understood all these things?” They said to him, “Yes.”

verses.rationale: Retains scribal learning and both new and old without replacing one with the other.
verses.before: He said to them, “Therefore every scribe trained for the kingdom of heaven is like a householder who brings out of the treasure things new and old.”
verses.after: He said to them, “So every scribe trained as a disciple of the kingdom of heaven is like a householder who brings out new things and old from his store.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to them, “Therefore every scribe who has been trained for the kingdom of heaven is like a master of a house, who brings out of his treasure what is new and what is old.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the formal discourse conclusion.
verses.before: When Jesus finished these parables, he left there.
verses.after: When Jesus finished these parables, he left that place.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when Jesus had finished these parables, he went away from there,

verses.rationale: Preserves the paired sources of astonishment.
verses.before: Coming to his hometown, he taught them in their synagogue, so that they were astonished and said, “Where did this man get this wisdom and these works of power?
verses.after: He came to his hometown and taught in their synagogue. They were astonished and said, “Where did this man get this wisdom and these mighty works?
verses.tsw_comparator: and coming to his hometown he taught them in their synagogue, so that they were astonished, and said, “Where did this man get this wisdom and these mighty works?

verses.rationale: Retains the trade, mother, and all four named brothers in source order.
verses.before: Is this not the carpenter's son? Is not his mother called Mary, and his brothers James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas?
verses.after: Isn’t this the carpenter’s son? Isn’t his mother called Mary, and aren’t his brothers James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas?
verses.tsw_comparator: Is not this the carpenter’s son? Is not his mother called Mary? And are not his brothers James and Joseph and Simon and Judas?

verses.rationale: Preserves the unnamed sisters and repeated origin question.
verses.before: And are not all his sisters with us? Where then did this man get all these things?”
verses.after: And aren’t all his sisters here with us? Then where did he get all this?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And are not all his sisters with us? Where then did this man get all these things?”

verses.rationale: Keeps the offense and the two exceptions to honor.

verses.after: As they left Jericho, a large crowd followed him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And as they went out of Jericho, a great crowd followed him.

verses.rationale: Keeps two and the royal mercy appeal.

verses.after: The crowd rebuked them, telling them to be quiet. But they cried out all the louder, “Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!”

verses.after: Jesus stopped, called them, and asked, “What do you want me to do for you?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And stopping, Jesus called them and said, “What do you want me to do for you?”

verses.after: When he entered Jerusalem, the whole city was shaken. “Who is this?” people asked.

verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to them, “It is written, ‘My house shall be called a house of prayer,’ but you are making it a den of robbers.”

verses.rationale: Preserves immediate sequence and perpetual prohibition without importing another chronology.

verses.tsw_comparator: And you say, ‘If anyone swears by the altar, it is nothing, but if anyone swears by the gift that is on the altar, he is bound by his oath.’

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned shorter address and repeats the sanctifying relation.
verses.before: Blind people! Which is greater—the gift, or the altar that makes the gift holy?
verses.after: Blind people! Which is greater: the gift, or the altar that makes the gift holy?
verses.tsw_comparator: You blind ones! For which is greater, the gift or the altar that makes the gift holy?

verses.rationale: Keeps the inclusive oath implication.
verses.before: Therefore, the one who swears by the altar swears by it and by everything on it.
verses.after: So whoever swears by the altar swears by it and by everything on it.
verses.tsw_comparator: So whoever swears by the altar swears by it and by everything on it,

verses.rationale: Preserves dwelling without replacing the personal referent with an abstraction.
verses.before: The one who swears by the temple swears by it and by the one who dwells in it.
verses.after: Whoever swears by the sanctuary swears by it and by the one who dwells in it.
verses.tsw_comparator: and whoever swears by the temple swears by it and by him who dwells in it,

verses.rationale: Keeps throne and enthroned person distinct in the image.
verses.before: And the one who swears by heaven swears by God's throne and by the one seated on it.
verses.after: And whoever swears by heaven swears by God’s throne and by the one seated on it.
verses.tsw_comparator: and whoever swears by heaven swears by the throne of God and by him who sits upon it.

verses.rationale: Retains all herbs, three virtues, and the nonexclusive conclusion.
verses.before: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! You tithe mint, dill, and cumin but have neglected the weightier matters of the Law—justice, mercy, and faithfulness. These you should have practiced without neglecting the others.
verses.after: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! You tithe mint, dill, and cumin, but have neglected the weightier matters of the Law: justice, mercy, and faithfulness. You should have practiced these without neglecting the others.
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you tithe mint and dill and cumin, and have neglected the weightier matters of the law: justice and mercy and faithfulness. These you ought to have done, without neglecting the others.

verses.rationale: Keeps the deliberately absurd size contrast.
verses.before: Blind guides! You strain out a gnat but swallow a camel!
verses.after: Blind guides! You strain out a gnat but swallow a camel.
verses.tsw_comparator: You blind guides, straining out a gnat and swallowing a camel!

verses.rationale: Follows pinned akrasia and preserves the image’s moral contents.
verses.before: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! You clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside they are full of greed and self-indulgence.
verses.after: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! You clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside they are full of plunder and self-indulgence.
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you clean the outside of the cup and the plate, but inside they are full of greed and self-indulgence.

verses.rationale: Keeps singular addressee, printed dish, and inside-before-outside sequence.
verses.before: Blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of the cup, so that the outside may also become clean.
verses.after: Blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of the cup and dish, so that its outside may become clean too.
verses.tsw_comparator: You blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of the cup and the plate, that the outside also may be clean.

verses.rationale: Preserves beauty/death contrast and ritual language.
verses.before: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! You are like whitewashed tombs, which appear beautiful on the outside but inside are full of dead people's bones and every kind of uncleanness.
verses.after: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! You are like whitewashed tombs, beautiful on the outside but full of dead people’s bones and every kind of uncleanness within.
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like whitewashed tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful, but within are full of dead bones and all uncleanness.

verses.rationale: Keeps the explicit interpretation of the tomb image.
verses.before: In the same way, on the outside you appear righteous to people, but inside you are full of hypocrisy and lawlessness.
verses.after: In the same way, you appear righteous to people on the outside, but inside you are full of hypocrisy and lawlessness.
verses.tsw_comparator: So you also outwardly appear righteous to others, but within you are full of hypocrisy and lawlessness.

verses.rationale: Preserves both commemorative activities.
verses.before: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! You build the tombs of the prophets and decorate the graves of the righteous,
verses.after: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! You build the prophets’ tombs and decorate the monuments of the righteous,
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you build the tombs of the prophets and decorate the monuments of the righteous,

verses.rationale: Keeps their counterfactual moral claim and blood imagery.
verses.before: and you say, ‘If we had lived in the days of our ancestors, we would not have shared with them in shedding the blood of the prophets.’
verses.after: and say, ‘If we had lived in our ancestors’ days, we would not have shared with them in shedding the prophets’ blood.’
verses.tsw_comparator: saying, ‘If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we would not have taken part with them in shedding the blood of the prophets.’

verses.rationale: Preserves the familial accusation as Jesus’ rhetorical argument.
verses.before: So you testify against yourselves that you are descendants of those who murdered the prophets.
verses.after: So you testify against yourselves that you are descendants of those who murdered the prophets.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus you bear witness against yourselves that you are sons of those who murdered the prophets.

verses.rationale: Retains the biting imperative and measure image without softening to prediction.
verses.before: Then fill up the measure of your ancestors!
verses.after: You too—fill up the measure of your ancestors!
verses.tsw_comparator: Fill up, then, the measure of your fathers.

verses.rationale: Keeps both insults and the rhetorical judgment question.
verses.before: Snakes! Brood of vipers! How will you escape the judgment of Gehenna?
verses.after: Snakes! Brood of vipers! How will you escape the judgment of Gehenna?
verses.tsw_comparator: You serpents, you brood of vipers, how are you to escape the judgment of Gehenna?

verses.rationale: Preserves all three sent groups and concrete forms of violence.
verses.before: “Therefore, look—I am sending you prophets, wise people, and scribes. Some of them you will kill and crucify, and some you will flog in your synagogues and persecute from town to town,
verses.after: That is why I am sending you prophets, wise people, and scribes. Some you will kill and crucify; others you will flog in your synagogues and persecute from town to town.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I send you prophets and wise men and scribes, some of whom you will kill and crucify, and some you will flog in your synagogues and persecute from town to town,

verses.rationale: Keeps the difficult patronymic exactly rather than harmonizing to another Zechariah.
verses.before: so that upon you may come all the righteous blood shed on earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Berechiah, whom you murdered between the sanctuary and the altar.
verses.after: So all the righteous blood shed on earth will come upon you, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Berechiah, whom you murdered between the sanctuary and the altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that on you may come all the righteous blood shed on earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Berechiah, whom you murdered between the sanctuary and the altar.

verses.rationale: Preserves this generation as the explicit scope.
verses.before: Truly I tell you, all these things will come upon this generation.
verses.after: Truly I tell you, all these things will come upon this generation.
verses.tsw_comparator: Truly, I say to you, all these things will come upon this generation.

verses.rationale: Retains doubled city name, maternal image, and competing wills.
verses.before: “Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those sent to you! How often I wanted to gather your children together the way a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were unwilling.
verses.after: “Jerusalem, Jerusalem! You kill the prophets and stone those sent to you. How often I wanted to gather your children as a hen gathers her chicks beneath her wings, but you were unwilling!
verses.tsw_comparator: “O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the city that kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to it! How often would I have gathered your children together as a hen gathers her brood under her wings, and you were not willing!

verses.rationale: Follows pinned deserted and leaves house’s referent open.
verses.before: Look, your house is left to you desolate.
verses.after: Look, your house is left to you deserted.
verses.tsw_comparator: See, your house is left to you desolate.

verses.rationale: Keeps the temporal qualification and exact earlier acclamation.
verses.before: For I tell you, you will not see me again until you say, ‘Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord.’”
verses.after: For I tell you, from now on you will not see me until you say, ‘Blessed is the one who comes in the Lord’s name.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: For I tell you, you will not see me again, until you say, ‘Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.’”
